# proc_macro2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/^1.0.106/

## Expand description

A wrapper around the procedural macro API of the compiler’s [ proc_macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/proc_macro/index.html)
crate. This library serves two purposes:

-
**Bring proc-macro-like functionality to other contexts like build.rs and main.rs.**Types from`proc_macro`are entirely specific to procedural macros and cannot ever exist in code outside of a procedural macro. Meanwhile`proc_macro2`types may exist anywhere including non-macro code. By developing foundational libraries like[syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn)and[quote](https://github.com/dtolnay/quote)against`proc_macro2`rather than`proc_macro`, the procedural macro ecosystem becomes easily applicable to many other use cases and we avoid reimplementing non-macro equivalents of those libraries.
-
**Make procedural macros unit testable.**As a consequence of being specific to procedural macros, nothing that uses`proc_macro`can be executed from a unit test. In order for helper libraries or components of a macro to be testable in isolation, they must be implemented using`proc_macro2`.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The skeleton of a typical procedural macro typically looks like this:

```
extern crate proc_macro;
#[proc_macro_derive(MyDerive)]
pub fn my_derive(input: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> proc_macro::TokenStream {
    let input = proc_macro2::TokenStream::from(input);
    let output: proc_macro2::TokenStream = {
        /* transform input */
    };
    proc_macro::TokenStream::from(output)
}
```
If parsing with [Syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn), you’ll use [ parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html) instead to
propagate parse errors correctly back to the compiler when parsing fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

The default feature set of proc-macro2 tracks the most recent stable
compiler API. Functionality in `proc_macro` that is not yet stable is not
exposed by proc-macro2 by default.

To opt into the additional APIs available in the most recent nightly
compiler, the `procmacro2_semver_exempt` config flag must be passed to
rustc. We will polyfill those nightly-only APIs back to Rust 1.68.0. As
these are unstable APIs that track the nightly compiler, minor versions of
proc-macro2 may make breaking changes to them at any time.

`RUSTFLAGS='--cfg procmacro2_semver_exempt' cargo build`Note that this must not only be done for your crate, but for any crate that depends on your crate. This infectious nature is intentional, as it serves as a reminder that you are outside of the normal semver guarantees.

Semver exempt methods are marked as such in the proc-macro2 documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#thread-safety)Thread-Safety

Most types in this crate are `!Sync` because the underlying compiler
types make use of thread-local memory, meaning they cannot be accessed from
a different thread.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [extra](https://docs.rs/extra/index.html)
- Items which do not have a correspondence to any API in the proc_macro crate, but are necessary to include in proc-macro2.
- [token_](https://docs.rs/token_stream/index.html)- stream
- Public implementation details for the `TokenStream`type, such as iterators.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Group](https://docs.rs/struct.Group.html)
- A delimited token stream.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [LexError](https://docs.rs/struct.LexError.html)
- Error returned from `TokenStream::from_str`.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineColumn.html)- Column - `span-locations`
- A line-column pair representing the start or end of a `Span`.
- [Literal](https://docs.rs/struct.Literal.html)
- A literal string (`"hello"`), byte string (`b"hello"`), character (`'a'`), byte character (`b'a'`), an integer or floating point number with or without a suffix (`1`,`1u8`,`2.3`,`2.3f32`).
- [Punct](https://docs.rs/struct.Punct.html)
- A `Punct`is a single punctuation character like`+`,`-`or`#`.
- [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)
- A region of source code, along with macro expansion information.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)- Stream
- An abstract stream of tokens, or more concretely a sequence of token trees.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Conversion](https://docs.rs/enum.ConversionErrorKind.html)- Error - Kind - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Error when retrieving a string literal’s unescaped value.
- [Delimiter](https://docs.rs/enum.Delimiter.html)
- Describes how a sequence of token trees is delimited.
- [Escape](https://docs.rs/enum.EscapeError.html)- Error - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Errors and warnings that can occur during string, char, and byte unescaping.
- [Spacing](https://docs.rs/enum.Spacing.html)
- Whether a `Punct`is followed immediately by another`Punct`or followed by another token or whitespace.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/enum.TokenTree.html)- Tree
- A single token or a delimited sequence of token trees (e.g. `[1, (), ..]`).

# quote - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/quote/^1.0.45/

## Expand description

This crate provides the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for turning Rust syntax tree data
structures into tokens of source code.

Procedural macros in Rust receive a stream of tokens as input, execute arbitrary Rust code to determine how to manipulate those tokens, and produce a stream of tokens to hand back to the compiler to compile into the caller’s crate. Quasi-quoting is a solution to one piece of that — producing tokens to return to the compiler.

The idea of quasi-quoting is that we write *code* that we treat as *data*.
Within the `quote!` macro, we can write what looks like code to our text
editor or IDE. We get all the benefits of the editor’s brace matching,
syntax highlighting, indentation, and maybe autocompletion. But rather than
compiling that as code into the current crate, we can treat it as data, pass
it around, mutate it, and eventually hand it back to the compiler as tokens
to compile into the macro caller’s crate.

This crate is motivated by the procedural macro use case, but is a general-purpose Rust quasi-quoting library and is not specific to procedural macros.

```
[dependencies]
quote = "1.0"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

The following quasi-quoted block of code is something you might find in [a](https://serde.rs/)
procedural macro having to do with data structure serialization. The `#var`
syntax performs interpolation of runtime variables into the quoted tokens.
Check out the documentation of the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for more detail about
the syntax. See also the

[macro which is important for implementing hygienic procedural macros.](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)

`quote_spanned!````
let tokens = quote! {
    struct SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        value: &'a #field_ty,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData<#item_ty>,
    }
    impl #generics serde::Serialize for SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
        where
            S: serde::Serializer,
        {
            #path(self.value, serializer)
        }
    }
    SerializeWith {
        value: #value,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData::<#item_ty>,
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#non-macro-code-generators)Non-macro code generators

When using `quote` in a build.rs or main.rs and writing the output out to a
file, consider having the code generator pass the tokens through
[prettyplease](https://github.com/dtolnay/prettyplease) before writing. This way if an error occurs in the generated
code it is convenient for a human to read and debug.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [format_](https://docs.rs/macro.format_ident.html)- ident
- Formatting macro for constructing `Ident`s.
- [quote](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html)
- The whole point.
- [quote_](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)- spanned
- Same as `quote!`, but applies a given span to all tokens originating within the macro invocation.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Ident](https://docs.rs/trait.IdentFragment.html)- Fragment
- Specialized formatting trait used by `format_ident!`.
- [ToTokens](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokens.html)
- Types that can be interpolated inside a `quote!`invocation.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/trait.TokenStreamExt.html)- Stream - Ext
- TokenStream extension trait with methods for appending tokens.

# syn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/syn/^2.0.117/

## Expand description

Syn is a parsing library for parsing a stream of Rust tokens into a syntax tree of Rust source code.

Currently this library is geared toward use in Rust procedural macros, but contains some APIs that may be useful more generally.

-
**Data structures**— Syn provides a complete syntax tree that can represent any valid Rust source code. The syntax tree is rooted at`syn::File``syn::Item``syn::Expr``syn::Type`
-
**Derives**— Of particular interest to derive macros is`syn::DeriveInput`
-
**Parsing**— Parsing in Syn is built around[parser functions](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)with the signature`fn(ParseStream) -> Result<T>`. Every syntax tree node defined by Syn is individually parsable and may be used as a building block for custom syntaxes, or you may dream up your own brand new syntax without involving any of our syntax tree types.
-
**Location information**— Every token parsed by Syn is associated with a`Span`that tracks line and column information back to the source of that token. These spans allow a procedural macro to display detailed error messages pointing to all the right places in the user’s code. There is an example of this below.
-
**Feature flags**— Functionality is aggressively feature gated so your procedural macros enable only what they need, and do not pay in compile time for all the rest.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-of-a-derive-macro)Example of a derive macro

The canonical derive macro using Syn looks like this. We write an ordinary
Rust function tagged with a `proc_macro_derive` attribute and the name of
the trait we are deriving. Any time that derive appears in the user’s code,
the Rust compiler passes their data structure as tokens into our macro. We
get to execute arbitrary Rust code to figure out what to do with those
tokens, then hand some tokens back to the compiler to compile into the
user’s crate.

```
[dependencies]
syn = "2.0"
quote = "1.0"
[lib]
proc-macro = true
```
```
use proc_macro::TokenStream;
use quote::quote;
use syn::{parse_macro_input, DeriveInput};
#[proc_macro_derive(MyMacro)]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    // Parse the input tokens into a syntax tree
    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
    // Build the output, possibly using quasi-quotation
    let expanded = quote! {
        // ...
    };
    // Hand the output tokens back to the compiler
    TokenStream::from(expanded)
}
```
The [ heapsize](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/heapsize) example directory shows a complete working implementation
of a derive macro. The example derives a

`HeapSize` trait which computes an
estimate of the amount of heap memory owned by a value.```
pub trait HeapSize {
    /// Total number of bytes of heap memory owned by `self`.
    fn heap_size_of_children(&self) -> usize;
}
```
The derive macro allows users to write `#[derive(HeapSize)]` on data
structures in their program.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Demo<'a, T: ?Sized> {
    a: Box<T>,
    b: u8,
    c: &'a str,
    d: String,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#spans-and-error-reporting)Spans and error reporting

The token-based procedural macro API provides great control over where the
compiler’s error messages are displayed in user code. Consider the error the
user sees if one of their field types does not implement `HeapSize`.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Broken {
    ok: String,
    bad: std::thread::Thread,
}
```
By tracking span information all the way through the expansion of a
procedural macro as shown in the `heapsize` example, token-based macros in
Syn are able to trigger errors that directly pinpoint the source of the
problem.

```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `std::thread::Thread: HeapSize` is not satisfied
 --> src/main.rs:7:5
  |
7 |     bad: std::thread::Thread,
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `HeapSize` is not implemented for `Thread`
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-custom-syntax)Parsing a custom syntax

The [ lazy-static](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/lazy-static) example directory shows the implementation of a

`functionlike!(...)` procedural macro in which the input tokens are parsed
using Syn’s parsing API.The example reimplements the popular `lazy_static` crate from crates.io as a
procedural macro.

```
lazy_static! {
    static ref USERNAME: Regex = Regex::new("^[a-z0-9_-]{3,16}$").unwrap();
}
```
The implementation shows how to trigger custom warnings and error messages on the macro input.

```
warning: come on, pick a more creative name
  --> src/main.rs:10:16
   |
10 |     static ref FOO: String = "lazy_static".to_owned();
   |                ^^^
```
[§](https://docs.rs#testing)Testing

When testing macros, we often care not just that the macro can be used
successfully but also that when the macro is provided with invalid input it
produces maximally helpful error messages. Consider using the [ trybuild](https://github.com/dtolnay/trybuild)
crate to write tests for errors that are emitted by your macro or errors
detected by the Rust compiler in the expanded code following misuse of the
macro. Such tests help avoid regressions from later refactors that
mistakenly make an error no longer trigger or be less helpful than it used
to be.

[§](https://docs.rs#debugging)Debugging

When developing a procedural macro it can be helpful to look at what the
generated code looks like. Use `cargo rustc -- -Zunstable-options -Zunpretty=expanded` or the [ cargo expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) subcommand.

To show the expanded code for some crate that uses your procedural macro,
run `cargo expand` from that crate. To show the expanded code for one of
your own test cases, run `cargo expand --test the_test_case` where the last
argument is the name of the test file without the `.rs` extension.

This write-up by Brandon W Maister discusses debugging in more detail:
[Debugging Rust’s new Custom Derive system](https://quodlibetor.github.io/posts/debugging-rusts-new-custom-derive-system/).

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

Syn puts a lot of functionality behind optional features in order to optimize compile time for the most common use cases. The following features are available.

- `derive`- *(enabled by default)*— Data structures for representing the possible input to a derive macro, including structs and enums and types.
- `full`
- `parsing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to parse input tokens into a syntax tree node of a chosen type.
- `printing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to print a syntax tree node as tokens of Rust source code.
- `visit`
- `visit-mut`
- `fold`
- `clone-impls`- *(enabled by default)*— Clone impls for all syntax tree types.
- `extra-traits`
- `proc-macro`- *(enabled by default)*— Runtime dependency on the dynamic library libproc_macro from rustc toolchain.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)- `parsing`
- A stably addressed token buffer supporting efficient traversal based on a cheaply copyable cursor.
- [ext](https://docs.rs/ext/index.html)
- Extension traits to provide parsing methods on foreign types.
- [fold](https://docs.rs/fold/index.html)- `fold`
- Syntax tree traversal to transform the nodes of an owned syntax tree.
- [meta](https://docs.rs/meta/index.html)- `parsing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Facility for interpreting structured content inside of an `Attribute`.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)- `parsing`
- Parsing interface for parsing a token stream into a syntax tree node.
- [punctuated](https://docs.rs/punctuated/index.html)
- A punctuated sequence of syntax tree nodes separated by punctuation.
- [spanned](https://docs.rs/spanned/index.html)- `parsing`and- `printing`
- A trait that can provide the `Span`of the complete contents of a syntax tree node.
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)
- Tokens representing Rust punctuation, keywords, and delimiters.
- [visit](https://docs.rs/visit/index.html)- `visit`
- Syntax tree traversal to walk a shared borrow of a syntax tree.
- [visit_](https://docs.rs/visit_mut/index.html)- mut - `visit-mut`
- Syntax tree traversal to mutate an exclusive borrow of a syntax tree in place.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [Token](https://docs.rs/macro.Token.html)
- A type-macro that expands to the name of the Rust type representation of a given token.
- [braced](https://docs.rs/macro.braced.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of curly braces and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [bracketed](https://docs.rs/macro.bracketed.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of square brackets and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_keyword.html)- keyword
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a given identifier as if it were a keyword.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_punctuation.html)- punctuation
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a multi-character symbol as if it were a punctuation token.
- [parenthesized](https://docs.rs/macro.parenthesized.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of parentheses and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_macro_input.html)- macro_ - input - `parsing`and- `proc-macro`
- Parse the input TokenStream of a macro, triggering a compile error if the tokens fail to parse.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote.html)- quote - `parsing`and- `printing`
- Quasi-quotation macro that accepts input like the `quote!`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote_spanned.html)- quote_ - spanned - `parsing`and- `printing`
- This macro is `parse_quote!``quote_spanned!`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/struct.Abi.html)- `derive`or- `full`

- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprParen.html)- Paren - `derive`or- `full`
- A parenthesized expression: `(a + b)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprPath.html)- Path - `derive`or- `full`
- A path like `core::mem::replace`possibly containing generic parameters and a qualified self-type.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRange.html)- Range - `full`
- A range expression: `1..2`,`1..`,`..2`,`1..=2`,`..=2`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRawAddr.html)- RawAddr - `full`
- Address-of operation: `&raw const place`or`&raw mut place`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprReference.html)- Reference - `derive`or- `full`
- A referencing operation: `&a`or`&mut a`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRepeat.html)- Repeat - `full`
- An array literal constructed from one repeated element: `[0u8; N]`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprReturn.html)- Return - `full`
- A `return`, with an optional value to be returned.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprStruct.html)- Struct - `derive`or- `full`
- A struct literal expression: `Point { x: 1, y: 1 }`.
- [ExprTry](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTry.html)- `full`
- A try-expression: `expr?`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTryBlock.html)- TryBlock - `full`
- A try block: `try { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTuple.html)- Tuple - `full`
- A tuple expression: `(a, b, c, d)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprUnary.html)- Unary - `derive`or- `full`
- A unary operation: `!x`,`*x`,`-x`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprUnsafe.html)- Unsafe - `full`
- An unsafe block: `unsafe { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprWhile.html)- While - `full`
- A while loop: `while expr { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprYield.html)- Yield - `full`
- A yield expression: `yield expr`.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.Field.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A field of a struct or enum variant.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldPat.html)- Pat - `full`
- A single field in a struct pattern.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldValue.html)- Value - `derive`or- `full`
- A field-value pair in a struct literal.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsNamed.html)- Named - `derive`or- `full`
- Named fields of a struct or struct variant such as `Point { x: f64, y: f64 }`.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsUnnamed.html)- Unnamed - `derive`or- `full`
- Unnamed fields of a tuple struct or tuple variant such as `Some(T)`.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.File.html)- `full`
- A complete file of Rust source code.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemFn.html)- Item - Fn - `full`
- A foreign function in an `extern`block.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within an extern block.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemStatic.html)- Item - Static - `full`
- A foreign static item in an `extern`block:`static ext: u8`.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- A foreign type in an `extern`block:`type void`.
- [Generics](https://docs.rs/struct.Generics.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Lifetimes and type parameters attached to a declaration of a function, enum, trait, etc.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplGenerics.html)- Generics - `printing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Returned by `Generics::split_for_impl`.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemConst.html)- Item - Const - `full`

- An associated function within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- An associated type within an impl block.
- [Index](https://docs.rs/struct.Index.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The index of an unnamed tuple struct field.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemConst.html)- Const - `full`
- A constant item: `const MAX: u16 = 65535`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemEnum.html)- Enum - `full`
- An enum definition: `enum Foo<A, B> { A(A), B(B) }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemExternCrate.html)- Extern - Crate - `full`
- An `extern crate`item:`extern crate serde`.
- [ItemFn](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemFn.html)- `full`
- A free-standing function: `fn process(n: usize) -> Result<()> { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemForeignMod.html)- Foreign - Mod - `full`

- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemImpl.html)- Impl - `full`

- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemStatic.html)- Static - `full`

- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemStruct.html)- Struct - `full`
- A struct definition: `struct Foo<A> { x: A }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemTrait.html)- Trait - `full`

- Data stored within an enum variant or struct.

- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/enum.ForeignItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item within an `extern`block.

- Unused, but reserved for RFC 3323 restrictions.

- Things that can appear directly inside of a module or scope.
- [Lit](https://docs.rs/enum.Lit.html)
- A Rust literal such as a string or integer or boolean.
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroDelimiter.html)- Delimiter - `derive`or- `full`
- A grouping token that surrounds a macro body: `m!(...)`or`m!{...}`or`m![...]`.
- [Member](https://docs.rs/enum.Member.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A struct or tuple struct field accessed in a struct literal or field expression.
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/enum.Meta.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Content of a compile-time structured attribute.
- [Pat](https://docs.rs/enum.Pat.html)- `full`
- A pattern in a local binding, function signature, match expression, or various other places.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/enum.PathArguments.html)- Arguments - `derive`or- `full`
- Angle bracketed or parenthesized arguments of a path segment.
- [Pointer](https://docs.rs/enum.PointerMutability.html)- Mutability - `full`
- Mutability of a raw pointer (`*const T`,`*mut T`), in which non-mutable isn’t the implicit default.
- [Range](https://docs.rs/enum.RangeLimits.html)- Limits - `full`

- [Return](https://docs.rs/enum.ReturnType.html)- Type - `derive`or- `full`

- [Static](https://docs.rs/enum.StaticMutability.html)- Mutability - `full`
- The mutability of an `Item::Static`or`ForeignItem::Static`.
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)- `full`
- A statement, usually ending in a semicolon.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.TraitBoundModifier.html)- Bound - Modifier - `derive`or- `full`
- A modifier on a trait bound, currently only used for the `?`in`?Sized`.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.TraitItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item declaration within the definition of a trait.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The possible types that a Rust value could have.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.TypeParamBound.html)- Param - Bound - `derive`or- `full`
- A trait or lifetime used as a bound on a type parameter.
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A unary operator: `*`,`!`,`-`.
- [UseTree](https://docs.rs/enum.UseTree.html)- `full`
- A suffix of an import tree in a `use`item:`Type as Renamed`or`*`.
- [Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The visibility level of an item: inherited or `pub`or`pub(restricted)`.
- [Where](https://docs.rs/enum.WherePredicate.html)- Predicate - `derive`or- `full`

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# fakecloud_account - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fakecloud-account/0.32.0/fakecloud_account/

## Expand description

AWS Account Management (`account`) restJson1 service for fakecloud.

The full 15-operation control plane from the AWS Smithy model: alternate
contacts (Get/Put/DeleteAlternateContact), primary contact information
(Get/PutContactInformation), account information (GetAccountInformation,
PutAccountName, GetGovCloudAccountInformation), primary-email management
(GetPrimaryEmail, Start/AcceptPrimaryEmailUpdate), and Region opt-in control
(ListRegions, GetRegionOptStatus, Enable/DisableRegion). Every operation is
backed by real, account-partitioned, persisted state and honors the optional
`AccountId` member so an organization’s management account can read/write a
member account’s settings.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use service::`- [AccountService](https://docs.rs/service/struct.AccountService.html);
- `pub use state::`- [AccountData](https://docs.rs/state/struct.AccountData.html);
- `pub use state::`- [ACCOUNT_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION](https://docs.rs/state/constant.ACCOUNT_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [persistence](https://docs.rs/persistence/index.html)
- Snapshot save/load for Account Management state.
- [service](https://docs.rs/service/index.html)
- Account Management restJson1 dispatch + operation handlers.
- [state](https://docs.rs/state/index.html)
- Account-partitioned, serializable state for AWS Account Management.

# md_tmpl_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/md-tmpl-macros/0.5.0/md_tmpl_macros/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#md-tmpl-macros)md-tmpl-macros

Proc macros for **build-time** template validation, pre-parsing, and
typed parameter struct generation for
[md-tmpl](https://github.com/domenukk/md-tmpl).

[§](https://docs.rs#why)Why?

The core `md-tmpl` crate validates at runtime. This companion
crate moves validation to `cargo build` — syntax errors, unknown
variables, and type mismatches become build errors. It also generates
typed Rust structs from frontmatter. Templates can still be loaded at
runtime for dynamic or hot-reload use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#installation)Installation

Available on crates.io: [https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl-macros](https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl-macros) (and [https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl](https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl))

```
cargo add md-tmpl
cargo add md-tmpl-macros
```
[§](https://docs.rs#macros)Macros

[§](https://docs.rs#include_template)`include_template!`

Reads, parses, and validates a `.tmpl.md` file at build time. Emits a
module with the pre-parsed template, typed parameter struct, sub-structs,
constants, and type aliases.

```
use md_tmpl_macros::include_template;
include_template!("prompts/simple_greeting.tmpl.md");
let output = simple_greeting::Params { name: "World".into() }
    .render()
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "\nHello World!\n");
```
Override the module name:

```
use md_tmpl_macros::include_template;
include_template!("prompts/simple_greeting.tmpl.md" => my_greet);
let output = my_greet::Params { name: "Alice".into() }
    .render()
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "\nHello Alice!\n");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generated-module-contents)Generated module contents

- `pub fn template() -> &'static Template`
- `pub struct Params { ... }`- `render()`— render using the embedded template.
- `render_reloaded(tmpl)`— render with an externally-loaded template (hot-reload).
- `validate_template(tmpl)`— check template compatibility.
- `to_context()`— convert to a- `Context`.

- Sub-structs for compound types (e.g. `ParamsItemsItem`).
- Constants from the `consts:`block.
- Type aliases / enums from the `types:`block.

[§](https://docs.rs#template)`template!`

Like `include_template!`, but for inline template strings. The
`=> module_name` is required.

```
md_tmpl_macros::template!(r#"
---
params:
  - name = str
---
Hello {{ name }}!
"# => greeting);
let output = greeting::Params { name: "World".into() }
    .render()
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "Hello World!\n");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hot-reload-with-type-safety)Hot-Reload with Type Safety

Combine build-time types with runtime loading — iterate on prompt wording without recompiling, while keeping your type guarantees:

```
use md_tmpl::Template;
md_tmpl_macros::include_template!("prompts/greeting.tmpl.md");
// Load from disk at runtime:
let tmpl = Template::from_file(std::path::Path::new("prompts/greeting.tmpl.md")).unwrap();
// Validate the reloaded file hasn't diverged:
greeting::Params::validate_template(&tmpl).unwrap();
// Render with the disk-loaded template:
let output = greeting::Params {
    name: "Bob".to_string(),
    count: 1,
    items: vec![],
}.render_reloaded(&tmpl).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#type-mapping)Type Mapping

| Frontmatter Type | Rust Type |
|---|---|
| `str` | `String` |
| `int` | `i64` |
| `float` | `f64` |
| `bool` | `bool` |
| `list(field = type, ...)` | `Vec<Params{Field}Item>`(auto-generated sub-struct) |
| `list(type)` | `Vec<RustType>`(e.g.`Vec<String>`) |
| `struct(field = type, ...)` | `Params{Field}`(auto-generated sub-struct) |
| `enum(Variant, ...)` | `Params{Field}`(auto-generated enum) |
| `option(T)` | `Option<RustType>` |
| `tmpl(field = type, ...)` | `Params{Field}`(template callable) |
| `tmpl()` | `Params{Field}`(template callable without args) |

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

Apache-2.0 OR MIT

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros-1)

- [include_](https://docs.rs/macro.include_template.html)- template
- Pre-parse and validate a `.tmpl.md`template at compile time and emit a complete module.
- [template](https://docs.rs/macro.template.html)
- Parse and validate an inline template string at compile time and emit a complete module.

# md_tmpl - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/md-tmpl/0.5.0/md_tmpl/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#md-tmpl)md-tmpl

Strongly-typed prompt templates for LLMs — markdown files with YAML frontmatter,
validated at **build time** via proc macros, with a full runtime API for dynamic loading.

```
use md_tmpl_macros::include_template;
// Parses and validates the template at build time, generates typed structs + enums.
include_template!("prompts/task_report.tmpl.md");
// Generated types:
//   task_report::Params                  — typed struct
//   task_report::ParamsPriority          — enum(Critical, High, Medium, Low)
//   task_report::ParamsTasksItem         — struct { name, urgency }
//   task_report::ParamsTasksItemUrgency  — enum(Critical, High, Medium, Low)
let params = task_report::Params::builder()
    .title("Deploy v2.0")
    .priority(task_report::ParamsPriority::Critical)
    .tasks([
        task_report::ParamsTasksItem::builder()
            .name("run migrations")
            .urgency(task_report::ParamsTasksItemUrgency::High)
            .build(),
        task_report::ParamsTasksItem::builder()
            .name("update load balancer")
            .urgency(task_report::ParamsTasksItemUrgency::Medium)
            .build(),
    ])
    .build();
let output = params.render().unwrap();
assert!(output.contains("# Task Report: Deploy v2.0"));
assert!(output.contains("Priority: Critical"));
assert!(output.contains("run migrations (High)"));
```
The template behind it — a plain `.tmpl.md` markdown file:

```
---
name: task_report
description: A task report template with types
types:
  - Priority = enum(Critical, High, Medium, Low)
params:
  - title = str
  - priority = Priority
  - tasks = list(name = str, urgency = Priority)
---
# Task Report: {{ title }}
Priority: {{ kind(priority) }}
> {% for task in tasks %}
- {{ task.name }} ({{ kind(task.urgency) }})
> {% /for %}
```
Rename a variant, add a field, remove a param — the compiler catches it immediately. No runtime surprises.

[§](https://docs.rs#why)Why?

- **Build-time validation**— proc macros parse and validate syntax, types, and variable references at- `cargo build`. Typos, missing fields, and type mismatches are build errors. Templates can also be loaded and validated at runtime.
- **Markdown-native**— prompts live in- `.tmpl.md`files, readable in any editor or on GitHub. Compound types use- `()`(never- `<>`), control-flow tags use- `> {% %}`blockquote prefixes.
- **Agent-safe**— when an LLM edits prompts, the compiler catches drift immediately.- `validate_template()`enables hot-reload with contract enforcement.

[§](https://docs.rs#installation)Installation

Available on crates.io: [https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl](https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl) (and [https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl-macros](https://crates.io/crates/md-tmpl-macros))

```
cargo add md-tmpl
# build-time validation + code generation:
cargo add md-tmpl-macros
```
**MSRV:** 1.85 (Rust 2024 edition) · ** no_std** compatible (disable default

`std` feature)[§](https://docs.rs#template-syntax--features)Template Syntax & Features

| Feature | Syntax / Example |
|---|---|
| Typed parameters | `str`,`int`,`float`,`bool`,`list(…)`,`struct(…)`,`enum(…)`,`option(…)`,`tmpl(…)` |
| Type aliases | `types:`block defines reusable named types (`Priority = enum(High, Low)`) |
| Cross-template imports | `imports:`pulls types via dotted paths (`stem.TypeName`) |
| Constants | `consts:`block for file-scoped immutable values |
| String interpolation | `{{ expr }}`inside all quoted strings — conditions, includes, panic messages |
| For loops & else | `> {% for task in tasks %} … > {% else %} empty > {% /for %}` |
| Conditionals | `> {% if count > 0 %} … > {% elif active %} … > {% else %} … > {% /if %}` |
| Enum dispatch | `> {% match status %} > {% case Approved %} … > {% case Rejected %} … > {% /match %}` |
| Includes as links | `> {% include [widget](widget.tmpl.md) with title = "Hello" %}` |
| Inline templates | `> {% tmpl header %} … > {% /tmpl %}`(call with`{% include header %}`) |
| Built-in functions | `idx(b)`,`len(x)`,`kind(x)`,`kinds(Type)`,`has(x)` |
| Filters | `upper`,`lower`,`trim`,`fixed(N)`,`join(sep)`,`limit(N)`,`add(N)`,`sub(N)` |

[§](https://docs.rs#build-time-typed-structs)Build-Time Typed Structs

[§](https://docs.rs#include_template)`include_template!`

Reads a `.tmpl.md` file at build time, validates it, and generates a typed
module:

```
use md_tmpl_macros::include_template;
// Generates: pub mod simple_greeting { pub struct Params { pub name: String } }
include_template!("prompts/simple_greeting.tmpl.md");
let output = simple_greeting::Params { name: "world".into() }.render().unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "\nHello world!\n");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#template)`template!`

Inline template strings — same validation, no file needed:

```
md_tmpl_macros::template!(r#"
---
params:
  - name = str
---
Hello {{ name }}!
"# => greeting);
let output = greeting::Params { name: "World".into() }
    .render()
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "Hello World!\n");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#typedbuilder-integration)`TypedBuilder` Integration

Enable `typed-builder` for ergonomic builder patterns:

```
cargo add md-tmpl --features typed-builder
cargo add md-tmpl-macros --features typed-builder
```
```
let params = greeting::Params::builder()
    .name("Alice")       // setter(into): accepts &str or String
    .count(42)
    .build();            // `items` defaults to vec![]
let output = params.render().unwrap();
```
| Field type | Builder behaviour |
|---|---|
| `String` | `setter(into)`— accepts`&str`,`String`, or anything`Into<String>` |
| `Vec<…>` | `default`— omit the field to get an empty`Vec` |
| Scalars ( `i64`,`f64`,`bool`) | Required |

Sub-structs also derive `TypedBuilder`:

```
let item = greeting::ParamsItemsItem::builder()
    .label("write docs")
    .build();
let params = greeting::Params::builder()
    .name("Alice")
    .count(1)
    .items(vec![item])
    .build();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#serde-integration)serde Integration

Render directly from any `Serialize` struct:

`cargo add md-tmpl --features serde````
use md_tmpl::Template;
use serde::Serialize;
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct ReviewParams {
    file_path: String,
    severity: String,
    findings: Vec<Finding>,
}
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Finding { line: i64, message: String }
let tmpl = Template::from_source("\
---
params:
  - file_path = str
  - severity = str
  - findings = list(line = int, message = str)
---
Severity: {{ severity }}
> {% for finding in findings %}
- Line {{ finding.line }}: {{ finding.message }}
> {% /for %}"
).unwrap();
let output = tmpl.render(&ReviewParams {
    file_path: "main.rs".into(),
    severity: "high".into(),
    findings: vec![
        Finding { line: 42, message: "unused variable".into() },
    ],
}).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-api)Runtime API

For dynamic or scripting use cases, parse templates at runtime.

[§](https://docs.rs#ctx-macro)`ctx!` Macro

Ergonomic context construction with nested structs and lists:

```
use md_tmpl::{ctx, Template};
let tmpl = Template::from_source("
---
params:
  - tasks = list(title = str, priority = str)
---
> {% for task in tasks %}
- **{{ task.title }}** ({{ task.priority }})
> {% /for %}"
).unwrap();
let output = tmpl.render_ctx(&ctx! {
    tasks: [
        { title: "Write documentation", priority: "High" },
        { title: "Add unit tests",      priority: "Medium" },
    ]
}).unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "- **Write documentation** (High)\n- **Add unit tests** (Medium)\n");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-loading)Runtime Loading

```
use md_tmpl::load_template;
let tmpl = load_template(std::path::Path::new("prompts"), "simple_greeting").unwrap();
let mut ctx = md_tmpl::Context::new();
ctx.set("name", "world");
let output = tmpl.render_ctx(&ctx).unwrap();
assert!(output.contains("Hello world!"));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#hot-reload)Hot-Reload

Load templates from disk at runtime while keeping type safety — iterate on prompt wording without recompiling:

```
let tmpl = md_tmpl::Template::from_file(
    std::path::Path::new("prompts/greeting.tmpl.md")
).unwrap();
greeting::Params::validate_template(&tmpl).unwrap();
let output = greeting::Params {
    name: "Bob".into(),
    count: 1,
    items: vec![],
}.render_reloaded(&tmpl).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#caching)Caching

`TemplateCache` hashes file contents — unchanged files return cached
compilations. `render_cached()` extends this to included templates:

```
use md_tmpl::TemplateCache;
let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
let path = dir.path().join("greeting.tmpl.md");
std::fs::write(&path, "\
---
params:
  - name = str
---
Hello {{ name }}!"
).unwrap();
let cache = TemplateCache::new();
let tmpl = cache.load(&path).unwrap();
let mut ctx = md_tmpl::Context::new();
ctx.set("name", "world");
let output = tmpl.render_ctx_cached(&ctx, &cache).unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, "Hello world!");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#defaults--extra-params)Defaults & Extra Params

[§](https://docs.rs#render_allowing_extra)`render_allowing_extra()`

Extra context keys not declared in frontmatter are silently ignored:

```
use md_tmpl::{ctx, Template};
let tmpl = Template::from_source("\
---
params:
  - name = str
---
Hello {{ name }}!"
).unwrap();
let ctx = ctx! { name: "world", extra_key: "ignored" };
assert_eq!(tmpl.render_ctx_allowing_extra(&ctx).unwrap(), "Hello world!");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#defaults_context)`defaults_context()`

Returns a `Context` pre-filled with default values:

```
use md_tmpl::Template;
let tmpl = Template::from_source("\
---
params:
  - name = str
  - count = int := 5
---
{{ name }} ({{ count }})"
).unwrap();
let mut ctx = tmpl.defaults_context();
ctx.set("name", "Alice"); // count already has default 5
assert_eq!(tmpl.render_ctx(&ctx).unwrap(), "Alice (5)");
```

[§](https://docs.rs#vs-competitors)vs Competitors

Criterion benchmarks, render only (pre-parsed template + data → output).
([source](https://docs.rs/benchmarks/benches/comparison.rs))

|---|---|---|---|---|
| simple | 150 ns🏆 | 216 ns | 554 ns | 673 ns |

| conditional | 211 ns🏆 | 343 ns | 623 ns | 1.38 µs |
| hero | 2.08 µs🏆 | 2.20 µs | 7.51 µs | 25.42 µs |
| mega | 8.64 µs🏆 | 10.89 µs | 28.49 µs | 88.99 µs |

```

# aerocontext_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-core/0.4.5/aerocontext_core/

## Expand description

Domain model and pluggable provider contract for aeronautical context.

This crate defines the provider-neutral types ([ model](https://docs.rs/model/index.html)) and the

[trait that every context-provider adapter implements (aviationweather.gov, Leidos Flight Service, future European sources). The assembled context serves a human pilot as a briefing and an AI agent as grounded, attributable context.](https://docs.rs/provider/trait.ContextProvider.html)

`ContextProvider`[§](https://docs.rs#capabilities)Capabilities

Every provider implements the [ ContextProvider](https://docs.rs/provider/trait.ContextProvider.html) identity trait, then
one capability trait per kind of context it serves:

- `WeatherBriefingProvider`
- `OwnshipStatusProvider`- `ControlCommandProvider`

Splitting by capability (not by provider) lets a new source — a future
European service, or a datalink source like FIS-B — implement only the
capabilities it offers, and lets each consumer depend only on the context
it needs. The weather data it returns ([ Briefing](https://docs.rs/model/struct.Briefing.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/model/struct.Product.html)

`Product`[) is](https://docs.rs/model/enum.ProductKind.html)

`model::ProductKind``#[non_exhaustive]`, so it grows without
breaking existing adapters.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use aircraft::`- [AircraftProfile](https://docs.rs/aircraft/struct.AircraftProfile.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [aircraft](https://docs.rs/aircraft/index.html)
- Pilot-supplied aircraft performance, the input a route brief needs to turn distance into time, altitude, and fuel.
- [command](https://docs.rs/command/index.html)
- The control-command capability.
- [compare](https://docs.rs/compare/index.html)
- Cross-source reconciliation of briefings with per-source attribution.
- [freshness](https://docs.rs/freshness/index.html)
- Provider-neutral data-freshness classification: `current`/`stale`/`unknown`, grounded in official product validities.
- [geo](https://docs.rs/geo/index.html)
- Spherical geodesy on `GeoPoint`
- [metar](https://docs.rs/metar/index.html)
- Decoded METAR observation fields and the FAA flight-rules category.
- [model](https://docs.rs/model/index.html)
- Provider-neutral briefing domain types.
- [navdata](https://docs.rs/navdata/index.html)
- Cycle-aware navigation-point data.
- [notam](https://docs.rs/notam/index.html)
- NOTAMs: the provider-neutral record, the query, the capability trait, and cross-source reconciliation.
- [ownship](https://docs.rs/ownship/index.html)
- The ownship-status capability.
- [provenance](https://docs.rs/provenance/index.html)
- The freshness/provenance envelope every agent-facing answer carries.
- [provider](https://docs.rs/provider/index.html)
- The shared context-provider identity contract.
- [route_](https://docs.rs/route_alert/index.html)- alert
- Route alerts: adverse-condition alerts (TFR, SIGMET, AIRMET, …) along a
planned route, as a neutral model plus the `RouteAlertProvider`
- [route_](https://docs.rs/route_request/index.html)- request
- The route-shaped briefing request: a corridor along an ordered set of waypoints, the seam that lets a provider answer for a whole flight instead of one area.
- [secret](https://docs.rs/secret/index.html)
- Credential primitives shared by every source adapter.
- [tfr](https://docs.rs/tfr/index.html)
- Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs): a neutral, source-agnostic model and
the `TfrProvider`
- [weather](https://docs.rs/weather/index.html)
- The weather-briefing capability.

- Per-job coordinator (JCP) pod naming and manifest helpers (WS-7.3).
- [lease](https://docs.rs/lease/index.html)
- K8s lease election.
- [pod_](https://docs.rs/pod_failure/index.html)- failure
- Executor pod launch failure detection.
- [pod_](https://docs.rs/pod_manager/index.html)- manager
- Kubernetes executor Pod lifecycle management (BUG-2).
- [queue_](https://docs.rs/queue_manager/index.html)- manager
- Queue CRD definitions for the krishiv operator.
- [reconciler](https://docs.rs/reconciler/index.html)
- Reconciliation.
- [status](https://docs.rs/status/index.html)
- KrishivJob status patching.
- [webhook](https://docs.rs/webhook/index.html)
- Kubernetes validating admission webhook for `KrishivJob`resources.

# krishiv_api - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/krishiv-api/0.1.0-nightly.202607030148/krishiv_api/

## Expand description

Public facade for `krishiv-api`.

High-level client API for constructing local, batch SQL, and streaming pipelines.

# krishiv_runtime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/krishiv-runtime/0.1.0-nightly.202607030148/krishiv_runtime/

## Expand description

Runtime traits and local backends for Krishiv.

Embedded mode runs batch SQL through the session `SqlEngine` (in `krishiv-api`).
Streaming plans are accepted here and executed via [ local_streaming](https://docs.rs/local_streaming/index.html) on
single-node backends (ADR-12.5).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use continuous_stream::`- [ContinuousStreamError](https://docs.rs/continuous_stream/enum.ContinuousStreamError.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [continuous_](https://docs.rs/continuous_stream/index.html)- stream
- Shared continuous streaming job state between session and in-process executor.
- [execution_](https://docs.rs/execution_runtime/index.html)- runtime
- Unified execution runtime across Embedded (in-process), SingleNode (local daemon), and Distributed modes.
- [flight_](https://docs.rs/flight_action/index.html)- action
- Typed Arrow Flight `DoAction`payloads for the Krishiv streaming control plane (B3, D2).
- [flight_](https://docs.rs/flight_client/index.html)- client
- Arrow Flight SQL client for `super::DistributedBackend`
- [flight_](https://docs.rs/flight_protocol/index.html)- protocol
- Krishiv Flight SQL comment protocol for catalog sync and remote streaming control.
- [in_](https://docs.rs/in_process/index.html)- process
- In-process coordinator + executor over shared mpsc/inbox transport (ADR-12.4).
- [in_](https://docs.rs/in_process_cluster/index.html)- process_ - cluster
- Session-scoped in-process coordinator + executor cluster (ADR-12.4 / ADR-13.3).
- [ivm_job](https://docs.rs/ivm_job/index.html)
- IVM job backends for remote and embedded modes.
- [local_](https://docs.rs/local_streaming/index.html)- streaming
- Bounded window execution (delegates to unified `krishiv-dataflow`operator runtime).
- [stream_](https://docs.rs/stream_kafka/index.html)- kafka
- Encode in-memory `RecordBatch``stream-kafka:`input partition descriptors.
- [streaming_](https://docs.rs/streaming_job/index.html)- job
- Ergonomic streaming job handle for the remote (coordinator HTTP) mode.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Distributed](https://docs.rs/struct.DistributedBackend.html)- Backend
- Distributed backend that routes plan execution to a remote coordinator via Arrow Flight SQL (GAP-RT-01 / ADR-12.3).
- [Embedded](https://docs.rs/struct.EmbeddedBackend.html)- Backend
- Embedded in-process backend: batch via session `SqlEngine`, streaming delegated to`SingleNodeBackend`
- [Execution](https://docs.rs/struct.ExecutionReport.html)- Report
- Minimal execution report for bootstrap backends.
- [IvmJob](https://docs.rs/struct.IvmJobRegistry.html)- Registry
- Registry of IVM jobs hosted on this coordinator process.
- [JobId](https://docs.rs/struct.JobId.html)
- Typed job id identifier.
- [JobStatus](https://docs.rs/struct.JobStatus.html)
- Minimal job status surfaced by `krishiv jobs`.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalJobRegistry.html)- JobRegistry
- Local in-memory job registry for bootstrap CLI/status behavior.
- [Remote](https://docs.rs/struct.RemoteStepSummary.html)- Step - Summary
- Summary returned by `execute_coordinator_ivm_step`
- [Single](https://docs.rs/struct.SingleNodeBackend.html)- Node - Backend
- Single-node in-process backend: accepts batch and streaming plans for local execution.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [IvmJob](https://docs.rs/enum.IvmJob.html)
- A coordinator-hosted IVM job: a single flow, or one auto-partitioned by key.
- [JobState](https://docs.rs/enum.JobState.html)
- Minimal job state for R1 local job listing.
- [Runtime](https://docs.rs/enum.RuntimeError.html)- Error
- Runtime errors shared by bootstrap backends and traits.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Execution](https://docs.rs/trait.ExecutionBackend.html)- Backend
- Runtime backend contract shared by embedded, single-node, and distributed modes.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_batch_sql.html)- coordinator_ - batch_ - sql
- Execute batch SQL via the coordinator using an async submit-then-poll pattern.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_batch_sql_inline.html)- coordinator_ - batch_ - sql_ - inline
- Execute batch SQL via the coordinator with **pre-encoded inline IPC**tables.

- Look up a single job by ID on the coordinator
(`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`).
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_checkpoint.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - checkpoint
- Retrieve a checkpoint from a remote IVM job.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_checkpoint_delta.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - checkpoint_ - delta
- Retrieve a delta checkpoint from a remote IVM job (deltas since last call).
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_create_job.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - create_ - job
- Create a new IVM job on the coordinator. Returns the assigned job ID.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_feed_source.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - feed_ - source
- Feed a `DeltaBatch`to a named source on a remote IVM job.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_feed_stream_delta.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - feed_ - stream_ - delta
- Feed a pre-computed `DeltaBatch`to a source on the coordinator (G4 fast path).
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_register_view.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - register_ - view
- Register or update an incremental view on a remote IVM job.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_restore.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - restore
- Restore an IVM job on the coordinator from checkpoint bytes.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_restore_delta.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - restore_ - delta
- Apply delta checkpoint bytes on a remote IVM job.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_snapshot.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - snapshot
- Retrieve the current materialized snapshot of a view from a remote IVM job.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_step.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - step
- Run one IVM tick on a remote job. Returns a `RemoteStepSummary`
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_ivm_stream_bridge.html)- coordinator_ - ivm_ - stream_ - bridge
- Push streaming micro-batch snapshots to an IVM source via the stream-bridge endpoint.
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_list_jobs.html)- coordinator_ - list_ - jobs
- List all jobs currently tracked by the coordinator (`GET /api/v1/jobs`).
- [execute_](https://docs.rs/fn.execute_coordinator_physical_plan.html)- coordinator_ - physical_ - plan
- Execute a physical plan on the coordinator via HTTP (batch SQL or continuous register).
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_streaming_plan.html)- streaming_ - plan
- Returns true when the plan must run through the single-node streaming runtime rather than DataFusion batch execution.
- [streaming_](https://docs.rs/fn.streaming_spec_from_plan.html)- spec_ - from_ - plan
- Derive a local window execution spec from typed streaming plan nodes.

# sim_lib_lang_ruby - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-ruby/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_ruby/

## Expand description

Ruby DSL surface profile for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the codec, eval-policy, and `Expr` contracts; this crate
is a loadable language profile presenting a Ruby surface syntax over the
shared `Expr` graph, not a standalone interpreter.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ruby](https://docs.rs/struct.RubyBlockScope.html)- Block - Scope
- A labeled Ruby block scope targeted by `break`and`next`exits.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_ruby_dsl_profile.html)- ruby_ - dsl_ - profile
- Installs the Ruby DSL profile and its organ claims into a registry.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_blocks_fidelity_symbol.html)- blocks_ - fidelity_ - symbol
- Stable symbol for the Ruby full-blocks fidelity badge (limited support).
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_break.html)- break
- Performs a Ruby `break`, escaping the block scope with`value`.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_conformance_test_symbol.html)- conformance_ - test_ - symbol
- Stable symbol for the Ruby DSL control conformance test.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_control_fidelity_symbol.html)- control_ - fidelity_ - symbol
- Stable symbol for the Ruby control-blocks fidelity badge.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_dispatch_fidelity_symbol.html)- dispatch_ - fidelity_ - symbol
- Stable symbol for the Ruby method-dispatch fidelity badge.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_dsl_matrix_row.html)- dsl_ - matrix_ - row
- Builds the Ruby DSL matrix row.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_dsl_profile.html)- dsl_ - profile
- Builds the `LanguageProfile`
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_dsl_source_cases.html)- dsl_ - source_ - cases
- Minimal source cases for the Ruby DSL matrix row.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_lowering_symbol.html)- lowering_ - symbol
- Stable symbol for the Ruby lowering from surface forms to `Expr`.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_next.html)- next
- Performs a Ruby `next`, advancing the block scope with`value`.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_profile_symbol.html)- profile_ - symbol
- Stable symbol identifying the Ruby DSL language profile.
- [ruby_](https://docs.rs/fn.ruby_reader_symbol.html)- reader_ - symbol
- Stable symbol for the reader codec the Ruby surface decodes through.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_ruby_dsl_conformance_case.html)- ruby_ - dsl_ - conformance_ - case
- Runs one Ruby DSL source conformance case.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_ruby_dsl_matrix_row.html)- ruby_ - dsl_ - matrix_ - row
- Runs the Ruby DSL matrix row and publishes claim-backed cells.

# krishiv_ui - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/krishiv-ui/0.1.0-nightly.202607030148/krishiv_ui/

## Expand description

R2 status API and server-rendered Web UI.

This crate exposes scheduler snapshots as a small Rust-native operations surface. It intentionally depends on the in-process R2 scheduler model rather than introducing Kubernetes clients or a separate frontend build.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [UiState](https://docs.rs/struct.UiState.html)
- Shared state for the R2 status server.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [UiError](https://docs.rs/enum.UiError.html)
- UI construction and handler errors.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [demo_](https://docs.rs/fn.demo_state.html)- state
- Create a deterministic demo state for local UI development and tests.
- [embedded_](https://docs.rs/fn.embedded_router.html)- router
- Build the UI-specific routes (jobs, executors, SQL editor, health dashboard) for embedding inside the coordinator HTTP server.
- [empty_](https://docs.rs/fn.empty_state.html)- state
- Create an empty active coordinator state for real status serving.
- [router](https://docs.rs/fn.router.html)
- Build the R2 UI router.
- [router_](https://docs.rs/fn.router_with_token.html)- with_ - token
- Build the R2 UI router with an explicit auth token. When `Some`, the same routes as`router()`get wrapped in the bearer-token middleware. When`None`, the router behaves identically to a`KRISHIV_UI_TOKEN`-unset build.
- [serve](https://docs.rs/fn.serve.html)
- Serve the R2 status API and Web UI with an existing listener.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [UiResult](https://docs.rs/type.UiResult.html)
- Shared UI result alias.

# plakat - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/plakat/1.22.0/plakat/

## Expand description

plakat — local text-to-image, style transfer, LoRA, upscale, and color-key CLI built on candle.

This crate is primarily consumed as the `plakat` binary defined in
`src/main.rs`. The library target exists so examples (under
`examples/`) and integration tests (under `tests/`) can reach into
the same module surface the binary uses, without duplicating
non-trivial code like CLIP-H preprocessing or model loading.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [artefacts](https://docs.rs/artefacts/index.html)
- Artefact compositing — place named PNG cutouts into named zones of a generated image.
- [capability](https://docs.rs/capability/index.html)
- `plakat doctor --capability`— which supported models can run on the detected hardware, at a glance.
- [civitai](https://docs.rs/civitai/index.html)
- v0.16 phase 7: Civitai browser + downloader.
- [cli](https://docs.rs/cli/index.html)
- [compile](https://docs.rs/compile/index.html)
- `plakat compile`— turn a prose- `prompts.txt`into a- `scenario`HJSON.
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- [device](https://docs.rs/device/index.html)
- [error_](https://docs.rs/error_hints/index.html)- hints
- v0.33 phase 1: actionable error hints.
- [hf](https://docs.rs/hf/index.html)
- [hw](https://docs.rs/hw/index.html)
- Hardware probe for `plakat doctor --capability`.
- [imaging](https://docs.rs/imaging/index.html)
- [instance_](https://docs.rs/instance_guard/index.html)- guard
- Single-instance guard — refuse to start a second heavy plakat run on the
same host. On unified-memory machines (Apple Silicon) two concurrent
model/training runs share the SAME memory pool and thrash each other into
swap (or trip the `crate::memwatch`
- [llm](https://docs.rs/llm/index.html)
- Local LLM-based prompt enhancer. Runs a small quantized
instruction-tuned model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct by default,
SmolLM2-360M-Instruct as a CPU-budget fallback) in-process via
candle’s `quantized_qwen2`/`quantized_llama`backends, so users get the v0.13 “enhance my prompt” workflow without an API key.
- [map](https://docs.rs/map/index.html)
- `plakat map`— scale-aware procedural fantasy maps. MAP-1 ships the spec + the LLM geographic parser; the geometry engine (MAP-2+) and the renderer (MAP-3/linework, MAP-6/tiled-SD) follow. See- `Documentation/RFC_MAP_COMPILE_PLAN.md`.
- [memwatch](https://docs.rs/memwatch/index.html)
- Memory watchdog — graceful self-abort before a unified-memory host crash.
- [pipelines](https://docs.rs/pipelines/index.html)
- [preset](https://docs.rs/preset/index.html)
- v0.25: art-style presets — `--look`(medium axis) +`--genre`(subject-domain axis).
- [prompt](https://docs.rs/prompt/index.html)
- [scripting](https://docs.rs/scripting/index.html)
- v0.21: Bund scripting language integration.
- [style](https://docs.rs/style/index.html)
- Art-style detection and transfer.
- [ui](https://docs.rs/ui/index.html)

# krishiv_scheduler - Rust

# krishiv_sql - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/krishiv-sql/0.1.0-nightly.202607030148/krishiv_sql/

## Expand description

SQL planning and local execution seam for Krishiv.

This crate owns the DataFusion integration for R1 while keeping DataFusion
out of the long-term public API exposed by `krishiv-api`.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use cep_sql::`- [MatchRecognizeStatement](https://docs.rs/cep_sql/struct.MatchRecognizeStatement.html);

- `pub use cep_sql::`- [parse_match_recognize](https://docs.rs/cep_sql/fn.parse_match_recognize.html);
- `pub use lakehouse::`- [AsOfTableRef](https://docs.rs/lakehouse/struct.AsOfTableRef.html);
- `pub use lakehouse::`- [MergeResult](https://docs.rs/lakehouse/struct.MergeResult.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [analyze](https://docs.rs/analyze/index.html)
- ANALYZE TABLE — collect column statistics from a batch.
- [catalog](https://docs.rs/catalog/index.html)
- Catalog abstractions for Krishiv.
- [cep_sql](https://docs.rs/cep_sql/index.html)
- `MATCH_RECOGNIZE`SQL extension planning and execution (R16 S2).
- [connector_](https://docs.rs/connector_table/index.html)- table
- DataFusion `TableProviderFactory`implementations backed by`krishiv_connectors::ConnectorRegistry`
- [create_](https://docs.rs/create_function_ddl/index.html)- function_ - ddl
- Pre-processor for `CREATE FUNCTION … RETURNS TABLE`DDL.
- [grammar](https://docs.rs/grammar/index.html)
- SQL grammar and feature matrix for Krishiv.
- [incremental_](https://docs.rs/incremental_view/index.html)- view
- `CREATE INCREMENTAL VIEW`and- `DECLARE RECURSIVE VIEW`SQL extensions.
- [introspection_](https://docs.rs/introspection_sql/index.html)- sql
- `DESCRIBE`,- `SHOW COLUMNS`, and- `EXPLAIN`SQL intercepts.
- [kafka_](https://docs.rs/kafka_table/index.html)- table
- [lakehouse](https://docs.rs/lakehouse/index.html)
- R18 lakehouse SQL extensions: delta/hudi providers, AS OF, MERGE INTO.
- [live_](https://docs.rs/live_table/index.html)- table
- `CREATE LIVE TABLE`SQL extensions (R14 S1.1).
- [pipeline_](https://docs.rs/pipeline_ddl/index.html)- ddl
- Declarative pipeline DDL: `CREATE SOURCE`/`CREATE SINK`/`START PIPELINE`.
- [pivot_](https://docs.rs/pivot_sql/index.html)- sql
- E5.4 — PIVOT / UNPIVOT SQL macro rewrite layer.
- [recursive_](https://docs.rs/recursive_cte/index.html)- cte
- E5.3 — Recursive CTE: iterative fixpoint execution.
- [spark_](https://docs.rs/spark_sql_ext/index.html)- sql_ - ext
- Spark SQL extensions: LATERAL VIEW, TABLESAMPLE, TRANSFORM, DESCRIBE EXTENDED, etc. Spark SQL feature extensions — pre-processors for SQL constructs that DataFusion doesn’t parse natively.
- [sqlstate](https://docs.rs/sqlstate/index.html)
- SQLSTATE code mapping for Krishiv SQL errors.
- [streaming](https://docs.rs/streaming/index.html)
- [streaming_](https://docs.rs/streaming_tvf/index.html)- tvf
- Streaming window table-valued functions: TUMBLE, HOP, SESSION.
- [streaming_](https://docs.rs/streaming_window_plan/index.html)- window_ - plan
- Compile a windowed streaming SQL query into a `WindowExecutionSpec`
- [subquery](https://docs.rs/subquery/index.html)
- E5.1 — Correlated subquery decorrelation: EXISTS/IN/scalar subquery analysis.
- [unnest_](https://docs.rs/unnest_sql/index.html)- sql
- E5.2 — LATERAL / UNNEST SQL pre-processing.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [batch_](https://docs.rs/fn.batch_size_from_env.html)- size_ - from_ - env
- Resolve the batch size from `KRISHIV_BATCH_SIZE`env var.
- [default_](https://docs.rs/fn.default_parallelism_from_env.html)- parallelism_ - from_ - env
- Resolve the default parallelism from `KRISHIV_TARGET_PARALLELISM`env var.
- [explain_](https://docs.rs/fn.explain_sql.html)- sql
- Create bootstrap `EXPLAIN`text for a SQL query.
- [explain_](https://docs.rs/fn.explain_sql_optimized.html)- sql_ - optimized
- Explain a SQL query including optimizer rule decisions.
- [explain_](https://docs.rs/fn.explain_sql_with_cost.html)- sql_ - with_ - cost
- Explain a SQL query and append a cost estimate from the provided cost model.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_public_expression.html)- public_ - expression
- Parse the stable SQL-expression subset into the same engine-owned AST used by Rust and Python.
- [plan_](https://docs.rs/fn.plan_sql.html)- sql
- Create a Krishiv logical plan wrapper for a SQL query without executing it.
- [pretty_](https://docs.rs/fn.pretty_batches.html)- batches
- Format Arrow batches for CLI and tests.
- [query_](https://docs.rs/fn.query_memory_limit_from_env.html)- memory_ - limit_ - from_ - env
- Resolve the default per-engine memory limit from the
`KRISHIV_QUERY_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES`environment variable.
- [referenced_](https://docs.rs/fn.referenced_table_names.html)- table_ - names
- Return all base table/relation names referenced by `query`.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_query_memory_limit_bytes.html)- query_ - memory_ - limit_ - bytes
- Resolve a per-engine DataFusion memory limit from a raw env var value.
`None`, unparseable, and zero values all mean “no limit” (the engine runs with DataFusion’s default unbounded pool).
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_streaming_match_recognize_limit.html)- streaming_ - match_ - recognize_ - limit
- Resolve the streaming MATCH_RECOGNIZE row cap from a raw env var value.
`None`and unparseable values fall back to the documented default of 100_000. Zero is rejected because it would mean “scan zero rows”.
- [streaming_](https://docs.rs/fn.streaming_match_recognize_limit_from_env.html)- match_ - recognize_ - limit_ - from_ - env
- Resolve the streaming MATCH_RECOGNIZE row cap from the
`KRISHIV_MATCH_RECOGNIZE_STREAMING_LIMIT`environment variable.
