# modulino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/modulino/0.3.0/modulino/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#modulino)Modulino

A hardware-agnostic, `no_std` Rust driver for Arduino Modulino breakout boards.

This crate provides drivers for the following Modulino devices:

- `Buttons`
- `Buzzer`
- `Pixels`
- `Distance`
- `Movement`
- `Knob`
- `Thermo`- `hs3003`
- `Joystick`
- `LatchRelay`
- `Vibro`
- `LedMatrix`
- `Pressure`
- `Light`

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use modulino::{Pixels, Color};
// Create a Pixels instance with your I2C bus
let mut pixels = Pixels::new(i2c)?;
// Set the first LED to red
pixels.set_color(0, Color::RED, 50)?;
// Apply the changes
pixels.show()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `defmt`: Enable- `defmt`debug formatting for error types

[§](https://docs.rs#hardware-requirements)Hardware Requirements

All Modulino devices communicate over I2C at 100kHz. They use the Qwiic/STEMMA QT connector standard for easy daisy-chaining.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [addresses](https://docs.rs/addresses/index.html)
- Default I2C addresses for Modulino devices.
- [pinstrap](https://docs.rs/pinstrap/index.html)
- Pinstrap address map for device type detection.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

[32](#32)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[33](#33)#[proc_macro_derive(StableAbi)]
[34](#34)pub fn derive_stable_abi(item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[35](#35)    let item = parse_macro_input!(item as Item);
[36](#36)    let (ident, generics) = match item {
[37](#37)        Item::Struct(s) => (s.ident, s.generics),
[38](#38)        Item::Enum(e) => (e.ident, e.generics),
[39](#39)        Item::Type(t) => (t.ident, t.generics),
[40](#40)        item => {
[41](#41)            return Error::new_spanned(
[42](#42)                item,
[43](#43)                "StableAbi can only be derived for struct, enum, or type alias",
[44](#44)            )
[45](#45)            .to_compile_error()
[46](#46)            .into();
[47](#47)        }
[48](#48)    };
[49](#49)    let generics = add_stable_abi_type_param_bounds(generics);
[50](#50)    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();
[51](#51)
[52](#52)    let expanded = quote! {
[53](#53)        #[automatically_derived]
[54](#54)        impl #impl_generics ::solana_frozen_abi::stable_abi::StableAbi for #ident #ty_generics #where_clause {
[55](#55)            fn random_with_context(
[56](#56)                rng: &mut (impl ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::RngCore + ?Sized),
[57](#57)                _ctx: (),
[58](#58)            ) -> Self {
[59](#59)                ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::Rng::random::<Self>(rng)
[60](#60)            }
[61](#61)        }
[62](#62)    };
[63](#63)    expanded.into()
[64](#64)}

[74](#74)pub fn derive_stable_abi_sample(item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {

[97](#97)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[98](#98)#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[99](#99)enum AbiSerializer {
[100](#100)    Bincode,
[101](#101)    Wincode,
[102](#102)}
[103](#103)
[104](#104)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[105](#105)impl AbiSerializer {
[106](#106)    fn from_lit_str(lit: &LitStr) -> Result<Self, Error> {
[107](#107)        match lit.value().as_str() {
[108](#108)            "bincode" => Ok(Self::Bincode),
[109](#109)            "wincode" => Ok(Self::Wincode),
[110](#110)            other => Err(Error::new(
[111](#111)                lit.span(),
[112](#112)                format!(
[113](#113)                    "unsupported `abi_serializer` value `{other}`; expected `bincode` or `wincode`"
[114](#114)                ),
[115](#115)            )),
[116](#116)        }
[117](#117)    }
[118](#118)
[119](#119)    fn name(self) -> &'static str {
[120](#120)        match self {
[121](#121)            Self::Bincode => "bincode",
[122](#122)            Self::Wincode => "wincode",
[123](#123)        }
[124](#124)    }
[125](#125)
[126](#126)    fn serialize_expr(self) -> TokenStream2 {
[127](#127)        match self {
[128](#128)            Self::Bincode => quote! { ::solana_frozen_abi::bincode },
[129](#129)            Self::Wincode => quote! { ::solana_frozen_abi::wincode },
[130](#130)        }
[131](#131)    }
[132](#132)}
[133](#133)
[134](#134)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[138](#138)fn parse_abi_serializers(expr: &Expr) -> Result<Vec<AbiSerializer>, Error> {
[139](#139)    fn lit_str(expr: &Expr) -> Result<&LitStr, Error> {
[140](#140)        match expr {
[141](#141)            Expr::Group(group) => lit_str(&group.expr),
[144](#144)            Expr::Lit(ExprLit {
[145](#145)                lit: Lit::Str(lit), ..
[146](#146)            }) => Ok(lit),
[147](#147)            other => Err(Error::new_spanned(
[148](#148)                other,
[149](#149)                "expected a string literal `abi_serializer` value",
[150](#150)            )),
[151](#151)        }
[152](#152)    }
[153](#153)
[154](#154)    match expr {
[155](#155)        Expr::Array(array) => {
[156](#156)            if array.elems.is_empty() {
[157](#157)                return Err(Error::new_spanned(
[158](#158)                    array,
[159](#159)                    "`abi_serializer` list must not be empty",
[160](#160)                ));
[161](#161)            }
[162](#162)            array
[163](#163)                .elems
[164](#164)                .iter()
[165](#165)                .map(|elem| AbiSerializer::from_lit_str(lit_str(elem)?))
[166](#166)                .collect()
[167](#167)        }
[168](#168)        expr => Ok(vec![AbiSerializer::from_lit_str(lit_str(expr)?)?]),
[169](#169)    }
[170](#170)}

[172](#172)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[173](#173)enum RoundtripTest {
[174](#174)    No,
[175](#175)    WireOnly,
[176](#176)    EqAndWire,
[177](#177)}
[178](#178)
[179](#179)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[180](#180)fn parse_roundtrip_test(value: Option<&LitStr>) -> Result<RoundtripTest, Error> {
[181](#181)    match value {
[182](#182)        None => Ok(RoundtripTest::WireOnly),
[183](#183)        Some(value) => match value.value().as_str() {
[184](#184)            "no" => Ok(RoundtripTest::No),
[185](#185)            "wire_only" => Ok(RoundtripTest::WireOnly),
[186](#186)            "eq_and_wire" => Ok(RoundtripTest::EqAndWire),
[187](#187)            _ => Err(Error::new_spanned(value, "unsupported `test_roundtrip` value; expected \"no\", \"wire_only\", or \"eq_and_wire\"")),
[188](#188)        },
[189](#189)    }
[190](#190)}

[192](#192)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[193](#193)fn filter_serde_attrs(attrs: &[Attribute]) -> bool {
[194](#194)    fn contains_skip(tokens: TokenStream2) -> bool {
[195](#195)        for token in tokens.into_iter() {
[196](#196)            match token {
[197](#197)                TokenTree::Group(group) => {
[198](#198)                    if contains_skip(group.stream()) {
[199](#199)                        return true;
[200](#200)                    }
[201](#201)                }
[202](#202)                TokenTree::Ident(ident) => {
[203](#203)                    if ident == "skip" {
[204](#204)                        return true;
[205](#205)                    }
[206](#206)                }
[207](#207)                TokenTree::Punct(_) | TokenTree::Literal(_) => (),
[208](#208)            }
[209](#209)        }
[210](#210)
[211](#211)        false
[212](#212)    }
[213](#213)
[214](#214)    for attr in attrs {
[215](#215)        if !attr.path().is_ident("serde") {
[216](#216)            continue;
[217](#217)        }
[218](#218)
[219](#219)        if contains_skip(attr.to_token_stream()) {
[220](#220)            return true;
[221](#221)        }
[222](#222)    }
[223](#223)
[224](#224)    false
[225](#225)}
[226](#226)
[227](#227)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[228](#228)fn filter_allow_attrs(attrs: &mut Vec<Attribute>) {
[229](#229)    attrs.retain(|attr| {
[230](#230)        let ss = &attr.path().segments.first().unwrap().ident.to_string();
[231](#231)        ss.starts_with("allow")
[232](#232)    });
[233](#233)}
[234](#234)
[235](#235)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[236](#236)struct StableAbiSampleOptions {
[237](#237)    with_expr: Option<TokenStream2>,
[238](#238)    ctx_expr: Option<TokenStream2>,
[239](#239)}
[240](#240)
[241](#241)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[242](#242)fn parse_stable_abi_sample_options(field: &syn::Field) -> Result<StableAbiSampleOptions, Error> {
[243](#243)    let mut with_expr: Option<TokenStream2> = None;
[244](#244)    let mut ctx_expr: Option<TokenStream2> = None;
[245](#245)    for attr in &field.attrs {
[246](#246)        if !attr.path().is_ident("stable_abi_sample") {
[247](#247)            continue;
[248](#248)        }
[249](#249)        attr.parse_nested_meta(|meta| {
[250](#250)            if meta.path.is_ident("with") {
[251](#251)                if with_expr.is_some() {
[253](#253)                    return Err(meta.error("duplicate `with` in `#[stable_abi_sample(...)]`"));
[254](#254)                }
[255](#255)                let value = meta.value()?.parse::<LitStr>()?;
[256](#256)                let expr = syn::parse_str::<Expr>(&value.value()).map_err(|err| {
[257](#257)                    Error::new(value.span(), format!("invalid `with` expression: {err}"))
[258](#258)                })?;
[259](#259)                with_expr = Some(quote! { #expr });
[260](#260)                Ok(())
[261](#261)            } else if meta.path.is_ident("ctx") {
[262](#262)                if ctx_expr.is_some() {
[264](#264)                    return Err(meta.error("duplicate `ctx` in `#[stable_abi_sample(...)]`"));
[265](#265)                }
[266](#266)                let expr = meta.value()?.parse::<Expr>()?;
[267](#267)                ctx_expr = Some(quote! { #expr });
[268](#268)                Ok(())
[269](#269)            } else {
[270](#270)                Err(meta.error(
[271](#271)                    "unsupported `stable_abi_sample` option; expected `with = \"...\"` or `ctx = <expr>`",
[272](#272)                ))
[273](#273)            }
[274](#274)        })?;
[275](#275)    }
[276](#276)    if with_expr.is_some() && ctx_expr.is_some() {
[277](#277)        return Err(Error::new_spanned(
[278](#278)            field,
[279](#279)            "cannot combine `with` and `ctx` in `#[stable_abi_sample(...)]`",
[280](#280)        ));
[281](#281)    }
[282](#282)    Ok(StableAbiSampleOptions {
[283](#283)        with_expr,
[284](#284)        ctx_expr,
[285](#285)    })
[286](#286)}
[287](#287)
[288](#288)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[289](#289)fn stable_abi_sample_field_expr(field: &syn::Field) -> Result<TokenStream2, Error> {
[290](#290)    let options = parse_stable_abi_sample_options(field)?;
[291](#291)    let ty = &field.ty;
[292](#292)    Ok(match (options.with_expr, options.ctx_expr) {
[293](#293)        (Some(expr), None) => expr,
[294](#294)        (None, Some(ctx_expr)) => quote! {
[295](#295)            <#ty as ::solana_frozen_abi::stable_abi::StableAbi<_>>::random_with_context(
[296](#296)                rng,
[297](#297)                #ctx_expr,
[298](#298)            )
[299](#299)        },
[300](#300)        (None, None) => {
[301](#301)            quote! {
[302](#302)                <#ty as ::solana_frozen_abi::stable_abi::StableAbi>::random(rng)
[303](#303)            }
[304](#304)        }
[305](#305)        (Some(_), Some(_)) => unreachable!("`with` and `ctx` are mutually exclusive"),
[306](#306)    })
[307](#307)}
[308](#308)
[309](#309)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[310](#310)fn add_stable_abi_type_param_bounds(mut generics: syn::Generics) -> syn::Generics {
[311](#311)    generics.type_params_mut().for_each(|type_param| {
[312](#312)        type_param.bounds.push(syn::parse_quote!(
[313](#313)            ::solana_frozen_abi::stable_abi::StableAbi
[314](#314)        ));
[315](#315)    });
[316](#316)    generics
[317](#317)}
[318](#318)
[319](#319)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[320](#320)fn derive_stable_abi_sample_struct_type(input: ItemStruct) -> Result<TokenStream2, Error> {
[321](#321)    let type_name = &input.ident;
[322](#322)    let generics = add_stable_abi_type_param_bounds(input.generics);
[323](#323)
[324](#324)    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();
[325](#325)    let turbofish = ty_generics.as_turbofish();
[326](#326)    let sample_expr = match &input.fields {
[327](#327)        Fields::Named(named_fields) => {
[328](#328)            let fields = named_fields
[329](#329)                .named
[330](#330)                .iter()
[331](#331)                .map(|field| -> Result<_, Error> {
[332](#332)                    let field_name = &field.ident;
[333](#333)                    let field_expr = stable_abi_sample_field_expr(field)?;
[334](#334)                    Ok(quote! {#field_name: #field_expr,})
[335](#335)                })
[336](#336)                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
[337](#337)            quote! {#type_name #turbofish { #(#fields)* }}
[338](#338)        }
[339](#339)        Fields::Unnamed(unnamed_fields) => {
[340](#340)            let fields = unnamed_fields
[341](#341)                .unnamed
[342](#342)                .iter()
[343](#343)                .map(stable_abi_sample_field_expr)
[344](#344)                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
[345](#345)            quote! {#type_name #turbofish ( #(#fields),* )}
[346](#346)        }
[347](#347)        Fields::Unit => quote! {#type_name #turbofish},
[348](#348)    };
[349](#349)    Ok(quote! {
[350](#350)        #[automatically_derived]
[351](#351)        impl #impl_generics ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::distr::Distribution<#type_name #ty_generics>
[352](#352)            for ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::distr::StandardUniform
[353](#353)            #where_clause
[354](#354)        {
[355](#355)            fn sample<R: ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::Rng + ?Sized>(
[356](#356)                &self,
[357](#357)                rng: &mut R,
[358](#358)            ) -> #type_name #ty_generics {
[359](#359)                #sample_expr
[360](#360)            }
[361](#361)        }
[362](#362)    })
[363](#363)}
[364](#364)
[365](#365)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[366](#366)fn stable_abi_sample_enum_variant_expr(
[367](#367)    type_name: &Ident,
[368](#368)    ty_generics: &syn::TypeGenerics,
[369](#369)    variant: &Variant,
[370](#370)) -> Result<TokenStream2, Error> {
[371](#371)    let variant_name = &variant.ident;
[372](#372)    let turbofish = ty_generics.as_turbofish();
[373](#373)    match &variant.fields {
[374](#374)        Fields::Unit => Ok(quote! {#type_name #turbofish::#variant_name}),
[375](#375)        Fields::Named(variant_fields) => {
[376](#376)            let fields = variant_fields
[377](#377)                .named
[378](#378)                .iter()
[379](#379)                .map(|field| -> Result<_, Error> {
[380](#380)                    let field_name = &field.ident;
[381](#381)                    let field_expr = stable_abi_sample_field_expr(field)?;
[382](#382)                    Ok(quote! {#field_name: #field_expr,})
[383](#383)                })
[384](#384)                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
[385](#385)            Ok(quote! {#type_name #turbofish::#variant_name { #(#fields)* }})
[386](#386)        }
[387](#387)        Fields::Unnamed(variant_fields) => {
[388](#388)            let fields = variant_fields
[389](#389)                .unnamed
[390](#390)                .iter()
[391](#391)                .map(stable_abi_sample_field_expr)
[392](#392)                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
[393](#393)            Ok(quote! {#type_name #turbofish::#variant_name( #(#fields),* )})
[394](#394)        }
[395](#395)    }
[396](#396)}
[397](#397)
[398](#398)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[399](#399)fn derive_stable_abi_sample_enum_type(input: ItemEnum) -> Result<TokenStream2, Error> {
[400](#400)    let type_name = &input.ident;
[401](#401)    let variants = &input.variants;
[402](#402)    let generics = add_stable_abi_type_param_bounds(input.generics);
[403](#403)
[404](#404)    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();
[405](#405)    let variant_count = variants.len();
[406](#406)    let match_arms = variants
[407](#407)        .iter()
[408](#408)        .enumerate()
[409](#409)        .map(|(index, variant)| -> Result<_, Error> {
[410](#410)            let sample_expr =
[411](#411)                stable_abi_sample_enum_variant_expr(type_name, &ty_generics, variant)?;
[412](#412)            Ok(quote! {#index => #sample_expr})
[413](#413)        })
[414](#414)        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
[415](#415)
[416](#416)    Ok(quote! {
[417](#417)        #[automatically_derived]
[418](#418)        impl #impl_generics ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::distr::Distribution<#type_name #ty_generics>
[419](#419)            for ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::distr::StandardUniform
[420](#420)            #where_clause
[421](#421)        {
[422](#422)            fn sample<R: ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::Rng + ?Sized>(
[423](#423)                &self,
[424](#424)                rng: &mut R,
[425](#425)            ) -> #type_name #ty_generics {
[426](#426)                match rng.random_range(0..#variant_count) {
[427](#427)                    #(#match_arms,)*
[428](#428)                    _ => unreachable!(),
[429](#429)                }
[430](#430)            }
[431](#431)        }
[432](#432)    })
[433](#433)}
[434](#434)
[435](#435)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[436](#436)fn derive_abi_sample_enum_type(input: ItemEnum) -> TokenStream {
[437](#437)    let type_name = &input.ident;
[438](#438)
[439](#439)    let mut sample_variant = quote! {};
[440](#440)    let mut sample_variant_found = false;
[441](#441)
[442](#442)    for variant in &input.variants {
[443](#443)        let variant_name = &variant.ident;
[444](#444)        let variant = &variant.fields;
[445](#445)        if *variant == Fields::Unit {
[446](#446)            sample_variant.extend(quote! {
[447](#447)                #type_name::#variant_name
[448](#448)            });
[449](#449)        } else if let Fields::Unnamed(variant_fields) = variant {
[450](#450)            let mut fields = quote! {};
[451](#451)            for field in &variant_fields.unnamed {
[452](#452)                if !(field.ident.is_none() && field.colon_token.is_none()) {
[453](#453)                    unimplemented!("tuple enum: {:?}", field);
[454](#454)                }
[455](#455)                let field_type = &field.ty;
[456](#456)                fields.extend(quote! {
[457](#457)                    <#field_type>::example(),
[458](#458)                });
[459](#459)            }
[460](#460)            sample_variant.extend(quote! {
[461](#461)                #type_name::#variant_name(#fields)
[462](#462)            });
[463](#463)        } else if let Fields::Named(variant_fields) = variant {
[464](#464)            let mut fields = quote! {};
[465](#465)            for field in &variant_fields.named {
[466](#466)                if field.ident.is_none() || field.colon_token.is_none() {
[467](#467)                    unimplemented!("tuple enum: {:?}", field);
[468](#468)                }
[469](#469)                let field_type = &field.ty;
[470](#470)                let field_name = &field.ident;
[471](#471)                fields.extend(quote! {
[472](#472)                    #field_name: <#field_type>::example(),
[473](#473)                });
[474](#474)            }
[475](#475)            sample_variant.extend(quote! {
[476](#476)                #type_name::#variant_name{#fields}
[477](#477)            });
[478](#478)        } else {
[479](#479)            unimplemented!("{:?}", variant);
[480](#480)        }
[481](#481)
[482](#482)        if !sample_variant_found {
[483](#483)            sample_variant_found = true;
[484](#484)            break;
[485](#485)        }
[486](#486)    }
[487](#487)
[488](#488)    if !sample_variant_found {
[489](#489)        unimplemented!("empty enum");
[490](#490)    }
[491](#491)
[492](#492)    let mut attrs = input.attrs.clone();
[493](#493)    filter_allow_attrs(&mut attrs);
[494](#494)    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = input.generics.split_for_impl();
[495](#495)
[496](#496)    let result = quote! {
[497](#497)        #[automatically_derived]
[498](#498)        #( #attrs )*
[499](#499)        impl #impl_generics ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_example::AbiExample for #type_name #ty_generics #where_clause {
[500](#500)            fn example() -> Self {
[501](#501)                ::std::println!(
[502](#502)                    "AbiExample for enum: {}",
[503](#503)                    std::any::type_name::<#type_name #ty_generics>()
[504](#504)                );
[505](#505)                #sample_variant
[506](#506)            }
[507](#507)        }
[508](#508)    };
[509](#509)    result.into()
[510](#510)}
[511](#511)
[512](#512)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[513](#513)fn derive_abi_sample_struct_type(input: ItemStruct) -> TokenStream {
[514](#514)    let type_name = &input.ident;
[515](#515)    let fields = &input.fields;
[516](#516)    let mut sample_fields = quote! {};
[517](#517)
[518](#518)    match fields {
[519](#519)        Fields::Named(_) => {
[520](#520)            for field in fields {
[521](#521)                let field_name = &field.ident;
[522](#522)                sample_fields.extend(quote! {
[523](#523)                    #field_name: AbiExample::example(),
[524](#524)                });
[525](#525)            }
[526](#526)            sample_fields = quote! {{ #sample_fields }};
[527](#527)        }
[528](#528)        Fields::Unnamed(_) => {
[529](#529)            for _ in fields {
[530](#530)                sample_fields.extend(quote! {
[531](#531)                    AbiExample::example(),
[532](#532)                });
[533](#533)            }
[534](#534)            sample_fields = quote! {( #sample_fields )};
[535](#535)        }
[536](#536)        _ => unimplemented!("fields: {:?}", fields),
[537](#537)    }
[538](#538)
[539](#539)    let mut attrs = input.attrs.clone();
[540](#540)    filter_allow_attrs(&mut attrs);
[541](#541)    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = input.generics.split_for_impl();
[542](#542)    let turbofish = ty_generics.as_turbofish();
[543](#543)
[544](#544)    let result = quote! {
[545](#545)        #[automatically_derived]
[546](#546)        #( #attrs )*
[547](#547)        impl #impl_generics ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_example::AbiExample for #type_name #ty_generics #where_clause {
[548](#548)            fn example() -> Self {
[549](#549)                ::std::println!(
[550](#550)                    "AbiExample::example for struct: {}",
[551](#551)                    std::any::type_name::<#type_name #ty_generics>()
[552](#552)                );
[553](#553)                use ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_example::AbiExample;
[554](#554)
[555](#555)                #type_name #turbofish #sample_fields
[556](#556)            }
[557](#557)        }
[558](#558)    };
[559](#559)
[560](#560)    result.into()
[561](#561)}

[563](#563)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[564](#564)#[proc_macro_derive(AbiExample)]
[565](#565)pub fn derive_abi_sample(item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[566](#566)    let item = parse_macro_input!(item as Item);

[568](#568)    match item {
[569](#569)        Item::Struct(input) => derive_abi_sample_struct_type(input),
[570](#570)        Item::Enum(input) => derive_abi_sample_enum_type(input),

[577](#577)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[578](#578)fn do_derive_abi_enum_visitor(input: ItemEnum) -> TokenStream {
[579](#579)    let type_name = &input.ident;
[580](#580)    let mut serialized_variants = quote! {};
[581](#581)    let mut variant_count: u64 = 0;
[582](#582)    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = input.generics.split_for_impl();
[583](#583)    for variant in &input.variants {
[584](#584)        if filter_serde_attrs(&variant.attrs) {
[586](#586)            continue;
[587](#587)        };
[588](#588)        let sample_variant = quote_sample_variant(type_name, &ty_generics, variant);
[589](#589)        variant_count = if let Some(variant_count) = variant_count.checked_add(1) {
[590](#590)            variant_count
[591](#591)        } else {
[592](#592)            break;
[593](#593)        };
[594](#594)        serialized_variants.extend(quote! {
[595](#595)            #sample_variant;
[596](#596)            Serialize::serialize(&sample_variant, digester.create_enum_child()?)?;
[597](#597)        });
[598](#598)    }
[599](#599)
[600](#600)    let type_str = format!("{type_name}");
[601](#601)    (quote! {
[602](#602)        impl #impl_generics ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_example::AbiEnumVisitor for #type_name #ty_generics #where_clause {
[603](#603)            fn visit_for_abi(&self, digester: &mut ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_digester::AbiDigester) -> ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_digester::DigestResult {
[604](#604)                let enum_name = #type_str;
[605](#605)                use ::serde::ser::Serialize;
[606](#606)                use ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_example::AbiExample;
[607](#607)                digester.update_with_string(::std::format!("enum {} (variants = {})", enum_name, #variant_count));
[608](#608)                #serialized_variants
[609](#609)                digester.create_child()
[610](#610)            }
[611](#611)        }
[612](#612)    }).into()
[613](#613)}

[628](#628)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[629](#629)fn quote_for_test(
[630](#630)    test_mod_ident: &Ident,
[631](#631)    type_name: &Ident,
[632](#632)    expected_api_digest: Option<&Expr>,
[633](#633)    expected_abi_digest: Option<&Expr>,
[634](#634)    abi_serializers: &[AbiSerializer],
[635](#635)    roundtrip_test: RoundtripTest,
[636](#636)) -> TokenStream2 {
[637](#637)    let test_api = if let Some(expected_api_digest) = expected_api_digest {
[638](#638)        quote! {
[639](#639)                #[test]
[640](#640)                fn test_api_digest() {
[641](#641)                    use ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_example::{AbiExample, AbiEnumVisitor};
[642](#642)
[643](#643)                    let mut digester = ::solana_frozen_abi::abi_digester::AbiDigester::create();
[644](#644)                    let example = <#type_name>::example();
[645](#645)                    let result = <_>::visit_for_abi(&&example, &mut digester);
[646](#646)                    let mut hash = digester.finalize();
[647](#647)                    if result.is_err() {
[648](#648)                        ::std::eprintln!("Error: digest error: {:#?}", result);
[649](#649)                    }
[650](#650)                    result.unwrap();
[651](#651)                    let actual_digest = ::std::format!("{}", hash);
[652](#652)                    if ::std::env::var("SOLANA_ABI_BULK_UPDATE").is_ok() {
[653](#653)                        if #expected_api_digest != actual_digest {
[654](#654)                            ::std::eprintln!("sed -i -e 's/{}/{}/g' $(git grep --files-with-matches frozen_abi)", #expected_api_digest, hash);
[655](#655)                        }
[656](#656)                        ::std::eprintln!("Warning: Not testing the abi digest under SOLANA_ABI_BULK_UPDATE!");
[657](#657)                    } else {
[658](#658)                        if let Ok(dir) = ::std::env::var("SOLANA_ABI_DUMP_DIR") {
[659](#659)                            assert_eq!(#expected_api_digest, actual_digest, "Possibly API changed? Examine the diff in SOLANA_ABI_DUMP_DIR!: \n$ diff -u {}/*{}* {}/*{}*", dir, #expected_api_digest, dir, actual_digest);
[660](#660)                        } else {
[661](#661)                            assert_eq!(#expected_api_digest, actual_digest, "Possibly API changed? Confirm the diff by rerunning before and after this test failed with SOLANA_ABI_DUMP_DIR!");
[662](#662)                        }
[663](#663)                    }
[664](#664)                }
[665](#665)        }
[666](#666)    } else {
[667](#667)        TokenStream2::new()
[668](#668)    };
[669](#669)
[670](#670)    let test_abi = if let Some(expected_abi_digest) = expected_abi_digest {
[674](#674)        let abi_tests = abi_serializers.iter().map(|abi_serializer| {
[675](#675)            let test_fn_name = Ident::new(
[676](#676)                &format!("test_abi_digest_{}", abi_serializer.name()),
[677](#677)                Span::call_site(),
[678](#678)            );
[679](#679)            let abi_serialize_expr = abi_serializer.serialize_expr();
[680](#680)            let test_roundtrip = match roundtrip_test {
[681](#681)                RoundtripTest::No => TokenStream2::new(),
[682](#682)                RoundtripTest::WireOnly | RoundtripTest::EqAndWire => {
[683](#683)                    let test_roundtrip_eq = match roundtrip_test {
[684](#684)                        RoundtripTest::EqAndWire => quote! {
[685](#685)                            assert!(
[686](#686)                                val == roundtrip_val,
[687](#687)                                "deserializing serialized {} should preserve value",
[688](#688)                                roundtrip_type_name
[689](#689)                            );
[690](#690)                        },
[691](#691)                        _ => TokenStream2::new(),
[692](#692)                    };
[693](#693)                    quote! {
[694](#694)                        let roundtrip_type_name = ::std::any::type_name::<#type_name>();
[695](#695)                        let roundtrip_val: #type_name =
[696](#696)                            #abi_serialize_expr::deserialize::<#type_name>(&bytes).expect(
[697](#697)                                ::std::concat!(
[698](#698)                                    "must deserialize serialized ",
[699](#699)                                    ::std::stringify!(#type_name)
[700](#700)                                )
[701](#701)                            );
[702](#702)
[703](#703)                        #test_roundtrip_eq
[704](#704)
[705](#705)                        let roundtrip_bytes = #abi_serialize_expr::serialize(&roundtrip_val).expect(
[706](#706)                            ::std::concat!(
[707](#707)                                "must re-serialize ",
[708](#708)                                ::std::stringify!(#type_name)
[709](#709)                            )
[710](#710)                        );
[711](#711)                        assert_eq!(
[712](#712)                            bytes,
[713](#713)                            roundtrip_bytes,
[714](#714)                            "re-serializing deserialized {} should match bytes",
[715](#715)                            roundtrip_type_name
[716](#716)                        );
[717](#717)                    }
[718](#718)                }
[719](#719)            };
[720](#720)            quote! {
[721](#721)                #[test]
[722](#722)                fn #test_fn_name() {
[723](#723)                    use ::solana_frozen_abi::rand::{SeedableRng, RngCore};
[724](#724)                    use ::solana_frozen_abi::rand_chacha::ChaCha8Rng;
[725](#725)                    use ::solana_frozen_abi::stable_abi::StableAbi;
[726](#726)
[727](#727)                    let mut rng = ChaCha8Rng::seed_from_u64(20666175621446498);
[728](#728)                    let mut digester = ::solana_frozen_abi::hash::Hasher::default();
[729](#729)
[730](#730)                    for _ in 0..10_000 {
[731](#731)                        let val = <#type_name>::random(&mut rng);
[732](#732)                        let bytes = #abi_serialize_expr::serialize(&val)
[733](#733)                            .expect("must serialize");
[734](#734)
[735](#735)                        #test_roundtrip
[736](#736)
[737](#737)                        digester.hash(&bytes);
[738](#738)                    }
[739](#739)                    assert_eq!(#expected_abi_digest, ::std::format!("{}", digester.result()), "ABI layout has changed!");
[740](#740)                }
[741](#741)            }
[742](#742)        });
[743](#743)        quote! { #(#abi_tests)* }
[744](#744)    } else {
[745](#745)        TokenStream2::new()
[746](#746)    };
[747](#747)
[748](#748)    quote! {
[749](#749)        #[cfg(test)]
[750](#750)        mod #test_mod_ident {
[751](#751)            use super::*;
[752](#752)            #test_api
[753](#753)            #test_abi
[754](#754)        }
[755](#755)    }

[811](#811)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[812](#812)fn quote_sample_variant(
[813](#813)    type_name: &Ident,
[814](#814)    ty_generics: &syn::TypeGenerics,
[815](#815)    variant: &Variant,
[816](#816)) -> TokenStream2 {
[817](#817)    let variant_name = &variant.ident;
[818](#818)    let variant = &variant.fields;
[819](#819)    if *variant == Fields::Unit {
[820](#820)        quote! {
[821](#821)            let sample_variant: #type_name #ty_generics = #type_name::#variant_name;
[822](#822)        }
[823](#823)    } else if let Fields::Unnamed(variant_fields) = variant {
[824](#824)        let mut fields = quote! {};
[825](#825)        for field in &variant_fields.unnamed {
[826](#826)            if !(field.ident.is_none() && field.colon_token.is_none()) {
[827](#827)                unimplemented!();
[828](#828)            }
[829](#829)            let ty = &field.ty;
[830](#830)            fields.extend(quote! {
[831](#831)                <#ty>::example(),
[832](#832)            });
[833](#833)        }
[834](#834)        quote! {
[835](#835)            let sample_variant: #type_name #ty_generics = #type_name::#variant_name(#fields);
[836](#836)        }
[837](#837)    } else if let Fields::Named(variant_fields) = variant {
[838](#838)        let mut fields = quote! {};
[839](#839)        for field in &variant_fields.named {
[840](#840)            if field.ident.is_none() || field.colon_token.is_none() {
[841](#841)                unimplemented!();
[842](#842)            }
[843](#843)            let field_type_name = &field.ty;
[844](#844)            let field_name = &field.ident;
[845](#845)            fields.extend(quote! {
[846](#846)                #field_name: <#field_type_name>::example(),
[847](#847)            });
[848](#848)        }
[849](#849)        quote! {
[850](#850)            let sample_variant: #type_name #ty_generics = #type_name::#variant_name{#fields};
[851](#851)        }
[852](#852)    } else {
[853](#853)        unimplemented!("variant: {:?}", variant)
[854](#854)    }
[855](#855)}
[856](#856)

[870](#870)        expected_abi_digest,

[881](#881)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[882](#882)#[proc_macro_attribute]
[883](#883)pub fn frozen_abi(attrs: TokenStream, item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[884](#884)    let mut api_expected_digest: Option<Expr> = None;
[885](#885)    let mut abi_expected_digest: Option<Expr> = None;
[886](#886)    let mut abi_serializers = vec![AbiSerializer::Bincode];
[887](#887)    let mut test_roundtrip: Option<LitStr> = None;
[888](#888)
[889](#889)    let attrs_parser = syn::meta::parser(|meta| {
[890](#890)        if meta.path.is_ident("digest") || meta.path.is_ident("api_digest") {
[891](#891)            api_expected_digest = Some(meta.value()?.parse::<Expr>()?);
[892](#892)            Ok(())
[893](#893)        } else if meta.path.is_ident("abi_digest") {
[894](#894)            abi_expected_digest = Some(meta.value()?.parse::<Expr>()?);
[895](#895)            Ok(())
[896](#896)        } else if meta.path.is_ident("abi_serializer") {
[897](#897)            abi_serializers = parse_abi_serializers(&meta.value()?.parse::<Expr>()?)?;
[898](#898)            Ok(())
[899](#899)        } else if meta.path.is_ident("test_roundtrip") {
[900](#900)            test_roundtrip = Some(meta.value()?.parse::<LitStr>()?);
[901](#901)            Ok(())
[902](#902)        } else {
[903](#903)            Err(meta.error("unsupported \"frozen_abi\" property"))
[904](#904)        }
[905](#905)    });
[906](#906)    parse_macro_input!(attrs with attrs_parser);
[907](#907)
[908](#908)    if api_expected_digest.is_none() && abi_expected_digest.is_none() {
[909](#909)        return Error::new_spanned(
[910](#910)            TokenStream2::from(item),
[911](#911)            "missing required attribute: #[frozen_abi(api_digest = \"...\" or abi_digest = \"...\")]",
[912](#912)        )
[913](#913)        .to_compile_error()
[914](#914)        .into();
[915](#915)    }
[916](#916)
[917](#917)    let roundtrip_test = match parse_roundtrip_test(test_roundtrip.as_ref()) {
[918](#918)        Ok(roundtrip_test) => roundtrip_test,
[919](#919)        Err(error) => return error.to_compile_error().into(),
[920](#920)    };
[921](#921)
[922](#922)    let item = parse_macro_input!(item as Item);
[923](#923)    match item {
[924](#924)        Item::Struct(input) => frozen_abi_struct_type(
[925](#925)            input,
[926](#926)            api_expected_digest.as_ref(),
[927](#927)            abi_expected_digest.as_ref(),
[928](#928)            &abi_serializers,
[929](#929)            roundtrip_test,
[930](#930)        ),
[931](#931)        Item::Enum(input) => frozen_abi_enum_type(
[932](#932)            input,
[933](#933)            api_expected_digest.as_ref(),
[934](#934)            abi_expected_digest.as_ref(),
[935](#935)            &abi_serializers,
[936](#936)            roundtrip_test,
[937](#937)        ),
[938](#938)        Item::Type(input) => frozen_abi_type_alias(
[939](#939)            input,
[940](#940)            api_expected_digest.as_ref(),
[941](#941)            abi_expected_digest.as_ref(),
[942](#942)            &abi_serializers,
[943](#943)            roundtrip_test,
[944](#944)        ),
[945](#945)        _ => Error::new_spanned(
[946](#946)            item,
[947](#947)            "frozen_abi isn't applicable; only for struct, enum and type",
[948](#948)        )
[949](#949)        .to_compile_error()
[950](#950)        .into(),
[951](#951)    }
[952](#952)}
[953](#953)
[954](#954)#[cfg(all(test, feature = "frozen-abi"))]
[955](#955)mod parse_abi_serializers_tests {
[956](#956)    use {
[957](#957)        super::*,
[958](#958)        AbiSerializer::{Bincode, Wincode},
[959](#959)    };
[960](#960)
[961](#961)    fn expr(input: &str) -> Expr {
[963](#963)        syn::parse_str(input).unwrap()
[964](#964)    }
[965](#965)
[966](#966)    #[test]
[967](#967)    fn valid_serializers() {
[968](#968)        assert_eq!(
[969](#969)            parse_abi_serializers(&expr(r#""bincode""#)).unwrap(),
[970](#970)            vec![Bincode]
[971](#971)        );
[972](#972)        assert_eq!(
[973](#973)            parse_abi_serializers(&expr(r#""wincode""#)).unwrap(),
[974](#974)            vec![Wincode]
[975](#975)        );
[976](#976)        assert_eq!(
[977](#977)            parse_abi_serializers(&expr(r#"["wincode"]"#)).unwrap(),
[978](#978)            vec![Wincode]
[979](#979)        );
[980](#980)        assert_eq!(
[981](#981)            parse_abi_serializers(&expr(r#"["bincode", "wincode"]"#)).unwrap(),
[982](#982)            vec![Bincode, Wincode]
[983](#983)        );
[984](#984)        assert_eq!(
[986](#986)            parse_abi_serializers(&expr(r#"["wincode", "bincode", "wincode"]"#)).unwrap(),
[987](#987)            vec![Wincode, Bincode, Wincode]
[988](#988)        );
[989](#989)    }
[990](#990)
[991](#991)    #[test]
[992](#992)    fn invalid_serializers_are_rejected() {
[993](#993)        let err = |input| parse_abi_serializers(&expr(input)).unwrap_err().to_string();
[994](#994)
[995](#995)        assert!(err(r#"[]"#).contains("must not be empty"));
[997](#997)
[998](#998)        assert!(err(r#""json""#).contains("unsupported"));
[1000](#1000)        assert!(err(r#""json""#).contains("json"));
[1001](#1001)        assert!(err(r#"["bincode", "json"]"#).contains("unsupported"));
[1002](#1002)
[1003](#1003)        assert!(err(r#"42"#).contains("expected a string literal"));
[1005](#1005)        assert!(err(r#"["bincode", 42]"#).contains("expected a string literal"));
[1006](#1006)    }
[1007](#1007)
[1008](#1008)    #[test]
[1009](#1009)    fn group_wrapped_literal_is_unwrapped() {
[1010](#1010)        let group = proc_macro2::Group::new(
[1014](#1014)            proc_macro2::Delimiter::None,
[1015](#1015)            expr(r#""wincode""#).to_token_stream(),
[1016](#1016)        );
[1017](#1017)        let grouped: Expr = syn::parse2(group.to_token_stream()).unwrap();
[1018](#1018)        assert!(matches!(grouped, Expr::Group(_)), "expected a grouped expr");
[1019](#1019)        assert_eq!(parse_abi_serializers(&grouped).unwrap(), vec![Wincode]);
[1020](#1020)    }

# proc-macro2 1.0.106 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/proc-macro2/^1.0.106

# proc-macro2

A wrapper around the procedural macro API of the compiler's `proc_macro` crate.
This library serves two purposes:

-
**Bring proc-macro-like functionality to other contexts like build.rs and main.rs.**Types from`proc_macro`are entirely specific to procedural macros and cannot ever exist in code outside of a procedural macro. Meanwhile`proc_macro2`types may exist anywhere including non-macro code. By developing foundational libraries like[syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn)and[quote](https://github.com/dtolnay/quote)against`proc_macro2`rather than`proc_macro`, the procedural macro ecosystem becomes easily applicable to many other use cases and we avoid reimplementing non-macro equivalents of those libraries.
-
**Make procedural macros unit testable.**As a consequence of being specific to procedural macros, nothing that uses`proc_macro`can be executed from a unit test. In order for helper libraries or components of a macro to be testable in isolation, they must be implemented using`proc_macro2`.

## Usage

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
The skeleton of a typical procedural macro typically looks like this:

```
extern crate proc_macro;
```
If parsing with [Syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn), you'll use [ parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html) instead to propagate
parse errors correctly back to the compiler when parsing fails.

## Unstable features

The default feature set of proc-macro2 tracks the most recent stable compiler
API. Functionality in `proc_macro` that is not yet stable is not exposed by
proc-macro2 by default.

To opt into the additional APIs available in the most recent nightly compiler,
the `procmacro2_semver_exempt` config flag must be passed to rustc. We will
polyfill those nightly-only APIs back to Rust 1.68.0. As these are unstable APIs
that track the nightly compiler, minor versions of proc-macro2 may make breaking
changes to them at any time.

```
RUSTFLAGS='--cfg procmacro2_semver_exempt' cargo build
```
Note that this must not only be done for your crate, but for any crate that depends on your crate. This infectious nature is intentional, as it serves as a reminder that you are outside of the normal semver guarantees.

Semver exempt methods are marked as such in the proc-macro2 documentation.

---

# quote 1.0.46 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/quote/^1.0.45

# Rust Quasi-Quoting

This crate provides the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0/quote/macro.quote.html) macro for turning Rust syntax tree data
structures into tokens of source code.

Procedural macros in Rust receive a stream of tokens as input, execute arbitrary Rust code to determine how to manipulate those tokens, and produce a stream of tokens to hand back to the compiler to compile into the caller's crate. Quasi-quoting is a solution to one piece of that — producing tokens to return to the compiler.

The idea of quasi-quoting is that we write *code* that we treat as *data*.
Within the `quote!` macro, we can write what looks like code to our text editor
or IDE. We get all the benefits of the editor's brace matching, syntax
highlighting, indentation, and maybe autocompletion. But rather than compiling
that as code into the current crate, we can treat it as data, pass it around,
mutate it, and eventually hand it back to the compiler as tokens to compile into
the macro caller's crate.

This crate is motivated by the procedural macro use case, but is a general-purpose Rust quasi-quoting library and is not specific to procedural macros.

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
## Syntax

The quote crate provides a [ quote!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0/quote/macro.quote.html) macro within which you can write Rust code
that gets packaged into a

[and can be treated as data. You should think of](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0/proc_macro2/struct.TokenStream.html)

`TokenStream``TokenStream` as representing a fragment of Rust source code.Within the `quote!` macro, interpolation is done with `#var`. Any type
implementing the [ quote::ToTokens](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0/quote/trait.ToTokens.html) trait can be interpolated. This includes
most Rust primitive types as well as most of the syntax tree types from

[.](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn)

`syn````
let tokens = quote! ;
```
## Repetition

Repetition is done using `#(...)*` or `#(...),*` similar to `macro_rules!`. This
iterates through the elements of any variable interpolated within the repetition
and inserts a copy of the repetition body for each one. The variables in an
interpolation may be a `Vec`, slice, `BTreeSet`, or any `Iterator`.

- `#(#var)*`— no separators
- `#(#var),*`— the character before the asterisk is used as a separator
- `#( struct #var; )*`— the repetition can contain other things
- `#( #k => println!("{}", #v), )*`— even multiple interpolations

Note that there is a difference between `#(#var ,)*` and `#(#var),*`—the latter
does not produce a trailing comma. This matches the behavior of delimiters in
`macro_rules!`.

## Returning tokens to the compiler

The `quote!` macro evaluates to an expression of type
`proc_macro2::TokenStream`. Meanwhile Rust procedural macros are expected to
return the type `proc_macro::TokenStream`.

The difference between the two types is that `proc_macro` types are entirely
specific to procedural macros and cannot ever exist in code outside of a
procedural macro, while `proc_macro2` types may exist anywhere including tests
and non-macro code like main.rs and build.rs. This is why even the procedural
macro ecosystem is largely built around `proc_macro2`, because that ensures the
libraries are unit testable and accessible in non-macro contexts.

There is a [ From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.From.html)-conversion in both directions so returning the output of

`quote!` from a procedural macro usually looks like `tokens.into()` or
`proc_macro::TokenStream::from(tokens)`.## Examples

### Combining quoted fragments

Usually you don't end up constructing an entire final `TokenStream` in one
piece. Different parts may come from different helper functions. The tokens
produced by `quote!` themselves implement `ToTokens` and so can be interpolated
into later `quote!` invocations to build up a final result.

```
let type_definition = quote! ;
let methods = quote! ;
let tokens = quote! ;
```
### Constructing identifiers

Suppose we have an identifier `ident` which came from somewhere in a macro
input and we need to modify it in some way for the macro output. Let's consider
prepending the identifier with an underscore.

Simply interpolating the identifier next to an underscore will not have the
behavior of concatenating them. The underscore and the identifier will continue
to be two separate tokens as if you had written `_ x`.

```
// incorrect
quote!
```
The solution is to build a new identifier token with the correct value. As this
is such a common case, the `format_ident!` macro provides a convenient utility
for doing so correctly.

```
let varname = format_ident!;
quote!
```
Alternatively, the APIs provided by Syn and proc-macro2 can be used to directly
build the identifier. This is roughly equivalent to the above, but will not
handle `ident` being a raw identifier.

```
let concatenated = format!;
let varname = new;
quote!
```
### Making method calls

Let's say our macro requires some type specified in the macro input to have a
constructor called `new`. We have the type in a variable called `field_type` of
type `syn::Type` and want to invoke the constructor.

```
// incorrect
quote!
```
This works only sometimes. If `field_type` is `String`, the expanded code
contains `String::new()` which is fine. But if `field_type` is something like
`Vec<i32>` then the expanded code is `Vec<i32>::new()` which is invalid syntax.
Ordinarily in handwritten Rust we would write `Vec::<i32>::new()` but for macros
often the following is more convenient.

```
quote!
```
This expands to `<Vec<i32>>::new()` which behaves correctly.

A similar pattern is appropriate for trait methods.

```
quote!
```
## Hygiene

Any interpolated tokens preserve the `Span` information provided by their
`ToTokens` implementation. Tokens that originate within a `quote!` invocation
are spanned with [ Span::call_site()](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0/proc_macro2/struct.Span.html#method.call_site).

A different span can be provided explicitly through the [ quote_spanned!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0/quote/macro.quote_spanned.html)
macro.

## Non-macro code generators

When using `quote` in a build.rs or main.rs and writing the output out to a
file, consider having the code generator pass the tokens through [prettyplease](https://github.com/dtolnay/prettyplease)
before writing. This way if an error occurs in the generated code it is
convenient for a human to read and debug.

Be aware that no kind of hygiene or span information is retained when tokens are written to a file; the conversion from tokens to source code is lossy.

Example usage in build.rs:

```
let output = quote! ;
let syntax_tree = parse2.unwrap;
let formatted = unparse;
let out_dir = var_os.unwrap;
let dest_path = new.join;
write.unwrap;
```

---

# syn 2.0.118 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/syn/^2.0.117

# Parser for Rust source code

Syn is a parsing library for parsing a stream of Rust tokens into a syntax tree of Rust source code.

Currently this library is geared toward use in Rust procedural macros, but contains some APIs that may be useful more generally.

-
**Data structures**— Syn provides a complete syntax tree that can represent any valid Rust source code. The syntax tree is rooted at`syn::File``syn::Item``syn::Expr``syn::Type`
-
**Derives**— Of particular interest to derive macros is`syn::DeriveInput`
-
**Parsing**— Parsing in Syn is built around[parser functions](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/parse/index.html)with the signature`fn(ParseStream) -> Result<T>`. Every syntax tree node defined by Syn is individually parsable and may be used as a building block for custom syntaxes, or you may dream up your own brand new syntax without involving any of our syntax tree types.
-
**Location information**— Every token parsed by Syn is associated with a`Span`that tracks line and column information back to the source of that token. These spans allow a procedural macro to display detailed error messages pointing to all the right places in the user's code. There is an example of this below.
-
**Feature flags**— Functionality is aggressively feature gated so your procedural macros enable only what they need, and do not pay in compile time for all the rest.

## Resources

The best way to learn about procedural macros is by writing some. Consider
working through [this procedural macro workshop](https://github.com/dtolnay/proc-macro-workshop) to get familiar with
the different types of procedural macros. The workshop contains relevant links
into the Syn documentation as you work through each project.

## Example of a derive macro

The canonical derive macro using Syn looks like this. We write an ordinary Rust
function tagged with a `proc_macro_derive` attribute and the name of the trait
we are deriving. Any time that derive appears in the user's code, the Rust
compiler passes their data structure as tokens into our macro. We get to execute
arbitrary Rust code to figure out what to do with those tokens, then hand some
tokens back to the compiler to compile into the user's crate.

```
[]
 = "2.0"
 = "1.0"
[]
 = true
```
```
use TokenStream;
use quote;
use ;
```
The [ heapsize](https://docs.rs/examples/heapsize) example directory shows a complete working implementation of a
derive macro. The example derives a

`HeapSize` trait which computes an estimate
of the amount of heap memory owned by a value.```
```
The derive macro allows users to write `#[derive(HeapSize)]` on data structures
in their program.

```
```
## Spans and error reporting

The token-based procedural macro API provides great control over where the
compiler's error messages are displayed in user code. Consider the error the
user sees if one of their field types does not implement `HeapSize`.

```
```
By tracking span information all the way through the expansion of a procedural
macro as shown in the `heapsize` example, token-based macros in Syn are able to
trigger errors that directly pinpoint the source of the problem.

```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `std::thread::Thread: HeapSize` is not satisfied
 --> src/main.rs:7:5
  |
7 |     bad: std::thread::Thread,
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `HeapSize` is not implemented for `std::thread::Thread`
```
## Parsing a custom syntax

The [ lazy-static](https://docs.rs/examples/lazy-static) example directory shows the implementation of a

`functionlike!(...)` procedural macro in which the input tokens are parsed using
Syn's parsing API.The example reimplements the popular `lazy_static` crate from crates.io as a
procedural macro.

```
lazy_static!
```
The implementation shows how to trigger custom warnings and error messages on the macro input.

```
warning: come on, pick a more creative name
  --> src/main.rs:10:16
   |
10 |     static ref FOO: String = "lazy_static".to_owned();
   |                ^^^
```
## Testing

When testing macros, we often care not just that the macro can be used
successfully but also that when the macro is provided with invalid input it
produces maximally helpful error messages. Consider using the [ trybuild](https://github.com/dtolnay/trybuild) crate
to write tests for errors that are emitted by your macro or errors detected by
the Rust compiler in the expanded code following misuse of the macro. Such tests
help avoid regressions from later refactors that mistakenly make an error no
longer trigger or be less helpful than it used to be.

## Debugging

When developing a procedural macro it can be helpful to look at what the
generated code looks like. Use `cargo rustc -- -Zunstable-options -Zunpretty=expanded` or the [ cargo expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) subcommand.

To show the expanded code for some crate that uses your procedural macro, run
`cargo expand` from that crate. To show the expanded code for one of your own
test cases, run `cargo expand --test the_test_case` where the last argument is
the name of the test file without the `.rs` extension.

This write-up by Brandon W Maister discusses debugging in more detail:
[Debugging Rust's new Custom Derive system](https://quodlibetor.github.io/posts/debugging-rusts-new-custom-derive-system/).

## Optional features

Syn puts a lot of functionality behind optional features in order to optimize compile time for the most common use cases. The following features are available.

- `derive`- *(enabled by default)*— Data structures for representing the possible input to a derive macro, including structs and enums and types.
- `full`
- `parsing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to parse input tokens into a syntax tree node of a chosen type.
- `printing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to print a syntax tree node as tokens of Rust source code.
- `visit`
- `visit-mut`
- `fold`
- `clone-impls`- *(enabled by default)*— Clone impls for all syntax tree types.
- `extra-traits`
- `proc-macro`- *(enabled by default)*— Runtime dependency on the dynamic library libproc_macro from rustc toolchain.

## Proc macro shim

Syn operates on the token representation provided by the [proc-macro2](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0/proc_macro2/) crate
from crates.io rather than using the compiler's built in proc-macro crate
directly. This enables code using Syn to execute outside of the context of a
procedural macro, such as in unit tests or build.rs, and we avoid needing
incompatible ecosystems for proc macros vs non-macro use cases.

In general all of your code should be written against proc-macro2 rather than
proc-macro. The one exception is in the signatures of procedural macro entry
points, which are required by the language to use `proc_macro::TokenStream`.

The proc-macro2 crate will automatically detect and use the compiler's data structures when a procedural macro is active.
